programs.amount: Free short appointments (typically half an hour) with a volunteer lawyer on almost any legal problem: family, wills and estates, debt, employment, housing, benefits, immigration. For people who cannot afford a lawyer and do not qualify for Legal Aid.
programs.eligibility_summary: You must live in BC, have a legal problem, meet the income guidelines (based on gross household income), and not be eligible for government-funded legal aid. Clinics run by phone and video across the province, including for Victoria and Vancouver Island residents.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Access Pro Bono: 1-877-762-6664.
Burnside Gorge Community Centre runs a free 15-minute phone legal clinic on Tuesdays 2 to 3 pm; book at 250-388-5251.
TAPS, 250-361-3521, for income assistance and tenancy.
Or call 211.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Call the client line at 604-878-7400, or toll-free 1-877-762-6664 (1-87-PROBONO-4) from outside Greater Vancouver.
2. Phone hours are Monday to Friday, 9:30 am to 12:30 pm and 1:30 pm to 4:30 pm, except holidays. You can leave a voicemail.
3. Or fill in the online intake ("triage") form at accessprobono.ca.
4. Staff check your eligibility and book you a free appointment with a lawyer, usually by phone.
programs.name: Access Pro Bono (free legal advice)
programs.phone_script: Access Pro Bono connects people in BC with a volunteer lawyer for a free advice session, if you can't afford a lawyer and don't qualify for Legal Aid. Call toll-free 1-877-762-6664, Monday to Friday, 9:30 to 12:30 or 1:30 to 4:30. You can also apply online at accessprobono.ca.

programs.amount: Free one-on-one help by phone or email to apply for the Disability Tax Credit, open a Registered Disability Savings Plan (RDSP), and understand the Canada Disability Benefit, trusts and estate planning. Access RDSP is a BC partnership of Plan Institute, Disability Alliance BC and BCANDS (Indigenous Disability Canada).
programs.eligibility_summary: Anyone in BC with a disability, or a family member or caregiver, who wants help with the RDSP or the Disability Tax Credit. Indigenous people in BC can get the same help from BCANDS, which is based in Victoria. There is no cost and no income test.
programs.help_in_victoria:
BCANDS (Indigenous Disability Canada), Victoria: 250-381-7303 / 1-888-815-5511.
Victoria Disability Resource Centre, 817A Fort Street, 250-595-0044.
Disability Alliance BC Access DTC: 1-800-663-1278.
Plan Institute helpline: 1-844-311-7526.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Call the Disability Planning Helpline at 1-844-311-7526 (toll-free, Canada-wide) or email helpline@planinstitute.ca.
2. Tell them whether you already have the Disability Tax Credit. If not, they will point you to an advocate (Disability Alliance BC) who helps with the T2201 form.
3. If you are Indigenous, call BCANDS in Victoria: 250-381-7303 or toll-free 1-888-815-5511.
4. Once the DTC is approved, the helpline walks you through opening an RDSP at a bank or credit union.
programs.name: Access RDSP / Plan Institute Disability Planning Helpline
programs.phone_script: Plan Institute runs a free helpline that walks you through the Disability Tax Credit and the Registered Disability Savings Plan, one on one. The toll-free number is 1-844-311-7526. If you are Indigenous, BCANDS in Victoria offers the same help at 250-381-7303.

programs.amount: Non-refundable. For the 2025 tax year: federal claim of $9,028 if your net income is $45,522 or less (smaller up to $105,709); BC claim of $5,799 if net income is $43,169 or less (smaller up to $81,829). The credit is worth roughly 14.5% of the federal amount and the BC rate of the BC amount in tax saved. Unused amount can move to your spouse.
programs.eligibility_summary: You were 65 or older on December 31 of the tax year and your net income (line 23600) is under $105,709 for the federal amount or under $81,829 for the BC amount (2025 tax year). You claim it on your tax return; no separate application.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Free tax clinics (CRA Community Volunteer Income Tax Program) for people with modest
income; see 211 for the nearest clinic and season.
Seniors Serving Seniors "Seniors Link" line: 250-413-3211. It is a message line checked
Monday to Friday, 9 am to 4 pm, and a volunteer calls you back (from sssbc.org).
Canada Revenue Agency individual tax enquiries: 1-800-959-8281 (TTY 1-800-665-0354).
programs.how_to_apply:
1. File your income tax return.
2. On the federal return enter the age amount on line 30100. If your net income is over $45,522, use the chart for line 30100 on the Federal Worksheet to get the reduced amount.
3. On form BC428 enter the BC age amount on line 58080 (use Worksheet BC428 if income is over $43,169).
4. If you cannot use all of it (low tax), transfer the rest to your spouse or common-law partner on their line 32600.
5. Free tax software and free tax clinics do this automatically when you enter your date of birth.
programs.name: Age amount tax credit (federal line 30100 and BC line 58080)
programs.phone_script: The age amount is a tax credit for people 65 and older; for the 2025 tax year it is up to $9,028 federally plus $5,799 for BC, and it lowers the tax you owe. There is no application: it is a line on your tax return, and a free tax clinic will put it in for you. If you cannot use all of it, your spouse can.

programs.amount: Up to $1,428.06 a month, tax-free (July to September 2026 rate), when your spouse gets GIS and full OAS and your combined 2025 income is under $42,144.
programs.eligibility_summary: You are 60 to 64, your spouse or common-law partner gets the Guaranteed Income Supplement, you are a Canadian citizen or legal resident, you have lived in Canada at least 10 years since age 18, your combined income is under $42,144 (2025 income, for July 2026 to June 2027 payments), and neither of you is under a sponsorship agreement. It stops the month after you turn 65, when you move to OAS and GIS yourself.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Seniors Serving Seniors "Seniors Link" line: 250-413-3211. It is a message line checked
Monday to Friday, 9 am to 4 pm, and a volunteer calls you back (from sssbc.org).
Service Canada: 1-800-277-9914 (TTY 1-800-255-4786).
For local form help, see 211, or ask for a Reachable Benefits navigator.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. You must apply; it is not automatic. Apply 6 to 11 months before you turn 60, or right away if you are already 60 to 64.
2. Online: sign in to My Service Canada Account, go to "Old Age Security", choose "Apply for Old Age Security and manage my benefits".
3. Paper: form ISP3008 (Application for the Allowance or Allowance for the Survivor) plus the income statement ISP3026. Mail both to Service Canada.
4. Have your SIN, your spouse's SIN and date of birth, the countries you have lived in since 18, and your bank details.
5. Both of you must file a tax return every year. The Allowance is recalculated every July.
programs.name: Allowance (for spouses aged 60 to 64 of GIS recipients)
programs.phone_script: The Allowance is a tax-free monthly payment for people aged 60 to 64 whose husband, wife or partner gets the Guaranteed Income Supplement. It can be up to about $1,428 a month right now, and you have to apply for it; it does not start on its own. Call Service Canada at 1-800-277-9914 and ask to apply for the Allowance.

programs.amount: Up to $1,702.34 a month, tax-free (July to September 2026 rate), if your 2025 income is under $30,696.
programs.eligibility_summary: You are 60 to 64, your spouse or common-law partner has died, you have not remarried or started a new common-law relationship, you are a Canadian citizen or legal resident, you have lived in Canada at least 10 years since age 18, your yearly income is under $30,696 (2025 income, for July 2026 to June 2027 payments), and you are not under a sponsorship agreement. It stops the month after you turn 65, when you move to OAS and GIS.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Seniors Serving Seniors "Seniors Link" line: 250-413-3211. It is a message line checked
Monday to Friday, 9 am to 4 pm, and a volunteer calls you back (from sssbc.org).
Service Canada: 1-800-277-9914 (TTY 1-800-255-4786).
For grief support and form help locally, see 211, or ask for a Reachable Benefits navigator.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. You must apply. If your spouse died before you turned 60, apply 6 to 11 months before your 60th birthday. If you are already 60 to 64, apply now.
2. Online: sign in to My Service Canada Account, go to "Old Age Security", choose "Apply for Old Age Security and manage my benefits".
3. Paper: form ISP3008 (Application for the Allowance or Allowance for the Survivor) plus income statement ISP3026. Mail both to Service Canada.
4. Have your late spouse's SIN, date of birth and date of death; the countries you have lived in since 18; and your bank details.
5. File a tax return every year. The benefit is recalculated every July.
programs.name: Allowance for the Survivor
programs.phone_script: The Allowance for the Survivor is a tax-free monthly payment for people aged 60 to 64 whose husband, wife or partner has died and who have a low income; it can be up to about $1,702 a month right now. You must apply for it, and it is separate from the CPP survivor's pension. Call Service Canada at 1-800-277-9914 and ask to apply for the Allowance for the Survivor.

programs.amount: Free, confidential information and referral to community, social and government services across BC: housing, food, mental health, financial help, legal help, seniors' and disability services and more. Reach it by phone, text or web chat in 13 languages.
programs.eligibility_summary: Anyone in BC. No cost, no eligibility test. Navigators help you find the right service near you and can give you the phone numbers and hours. It is the best fallback when no one else knows who to call.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Dial 2-1-1.
For seniors specifically: Seniors Serving Seniors line 250-413-3211.
For people with disabilities: Victoria Disability Resource Centre 250-595-0044.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Dial 2-1-1 from any phone, or text 2-1-1.
2. Or use the live chat or search the directory at bc.211.ca.
3. Phone and chat are staffed 9 am to 9 pm on weekdays (not holidays). The online directory works any time.
4. Tell the navigator what you need and where you live; they search for you and give you the details.
programs.name: 211 BC (community services helpline)
programs.phone_script: If you're not sure who to call, dial 2-1-1. It's a free, confidential helpline that finds community and government services near you: housing, food, benefits, legal help and more. They answer 9 am to 9 pm on weekdays, and you can also text 2-1-1 or chat at bc.211.ca.

programs.amount: Free annual bus pass for people with PWD on disability assistance (or take $52 a month in cash instead). Low-income seniors pay a $45 yearly fee (rate table effective August 1, 2026).
programs.eligibility_summary: You have the PWD designation and receive disability or hardship assistance from the ministry, or you are a low-income senior: 65 or older and receiving Old Age Security plus the Guaranteed Income Supplement, the Allowance or Allowance for the Survivor, or 60 or older on income assistance, or 60 or older and the spouse of a PWD recipient.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Together Against Poverty Society (TAPS), 828 View Street, Victoria. Phone 250-361-3521
(help with ministry benefits).
For other help, call 211.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Ask by the 5th of the month so it starts with the next payment.
2. Quickest: My Self Serve, Service Request tab, or the online form at myselfserve.gov.bc.ca/BusPass.
3. Or call 1-866-866-0800 (Monday to Friday, 9 am to 4 pm).
4. Seniors get an invoice for the $45 yearly fee; PWD recipients pay nothing.
5. Allow up to 6 weeks for the pass to arrive.
programs.name: BC Bus Pass Program
programs.phone_script: If you get B.C. disability assistance, you can have a free yearly bus pass, or $52 a month in cash instead. Low-income seniors who get the Guaranteed Income Supplement can buy the same pass for $45 a year. Call 1-866-866-0800 before the 5th of the month to ask for it.

programs.amount: One-time emergency payment for people already on income, disability, or hardship assistance. Food: up to $50 per person per month. Clothing: up to $110 per person per year (for example, up to $440 for a family of four in 12 months). Shelter: actual cost up to the combined support and shelter rate for your family size, normally once a year. Rates effective August 1, 2026.
programs.eligibility_summary: You get income assistance, disability assistance, or hardship assistance, and you face an unexpected expense, have no money or assets to cover it, and going without would put someone's health in immediate danger or lead to a child being removed. It can also cover things like a bed, emergency repairs, or essential utilities, not just food, clothing and rent.
programs.help_in_victoria: Together Against Poverty Society (TAPS), 828 View Street, Victoria. Phone 250-361-3521. TAPS advocates help people on assistance request supplements and appeal refusals. Or dial 2-1-1.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Ask your ministry worker right away: online through My Self Serve, by phone at 1-866-866-0800, or in person at a ministry or Service BC office.
2. Explain what happened, why it was unexpected, why you cannot pay, and what will happen to your health or your children if you go without.
3. Bring proof if you can (an eviction notice, a repair quote, a letter).
4. If refused, you can ask for reconsideration. An advocate can help.
programs.name: BC Crisis Supplement
programs.phone_script: If you're on income or disability assistance and something unexpected happens that you can't pay for, you can ask the ministry for a crisis supplement. It's a one-time payment for food, clothing, rent, or things like an emergency repair. Call 1-866-866-0800, say the words 'crisis supplement,' and explain why going without would harm your health.

programs.amount: 50% off the passenger fare on BC Ferries for a BC resident with a permanent disability, and 50% off for one personal attendant aged 12 or older if you need one. The vehicle fare is not discounted. A CNIB card gives the same discount.
programs.eligibility_summary: BC residents with a permanent disability, age 5 and up. If you receive the BC Persons with Disabilities (PWD) benefit or CPP Disability, proof of that is enough. Otherwise a medical practitioner must fill in Section C of the application. The card must be renewed every two years.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Victoria Disability Resource Centre, 817A Fort Street, 250-595-0044, helps with the form.
BC Ferries customer service: 1-888-223-3779.
Or call 211.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Download the AFI card application form from bcferries.com/accessibility, or call 1-888-223-3779 (1-888-BC-FERRY) to ask for one.
2. Attach proof of PWD or CPP-D, or have your doctor or nurse practitioner complete Section C.
3. Send the form back as the form directs (submission method was not shown on the page fetched: check current details).
4. Show the AFI card (or a CNIB card) to the ticket agent each time you sail. Renew every two years.
programs.name: BC Ferries Accessible Fare Identification (AFI) card (formerly the Disabled Card)
programs.phone_script: If you have a permanent disability and live in BC, BC Ferries gives you half price on your passenger fare, and half price for one helper who travels with you. You apply for an Accessible Fare Identification card; if you get PWD or CPP Disability that's all the proof you need. Call BC Ferries at 1-888-223-3779 or the Disability Resource Centre at 250-595-0044 for help.

programs.amount: Up to $500 back each calendar year in provincial fuel tax for one registered vehicle, plus 25% off ICBC basic Autoplan insurance.
programs.eligibility_summary: You own or lease a vehicle (or have an ownership interest in one) and you can confirm your disability with one of the accepted documents, such as a B.C. Disability Assistance certification, a CNIB letter, a Veterans Affairs letter for a 100% disability pension, or a medical certificate for a qualifying condition.
programs.help_in_victoria: Call 211 for a community agency that helps with forms. The program office is in Victoria at 250-410-0373.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Register once with form FIN 119 (Fuel Tax Refund Program Registration) and attach your proof of disability.
2. Once registered, keep your original fuel receipts.
3. Once your registration is approved, the program gives you the refund application form. Fill it in and mail it with the receipts.
4. Claims must arrive within four years of the date you paid the tax.
5. Show your registration to ICBC or your Autoplan broker for the 25% discount.
programs.name: BC Fuel Tax Refund for Persons with Disabilities
programs.phone_script: If you have a disability and a vehicle in your name, B.C. will refund up to $500 a year of the fuel tax you pay, and give you 25% off basic ICBC insurance. You register once with form FIN 119, then send in your gas receipts with the refund form they give you. The number is 1-877-388-4440.

programs.amount: Temporary monthly support for people who do not qualify for regular income or disability assistance. Paid one month at a time; amounts follow the income assistance rate table. Some categories must be repaid later.
programs.eligibility_summary: People in BC who are turned down for income or disability assistance for a specific reason but have used up every other way to meet basic needs. Categories: waiting for EI, waiting for other income (CPP, OAS, WorkSafe, veterans), assets or income over the limit (families with children), strike or lockout, immediate need with a work search, identity not yet proven, or waiting for a Social Insurance Number.
programs.help_in_victoria: Together Against Poverty Society (TAPS), 828 View Street, Victoria. Phone 250-361-3521. TAPS advocates help with income assistance applications, hardship claims, and appeals. Or dial 2-1-1.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Apply for income assistance first (online at My Self Serve, by phone at 1-866-866-0800, or in person). Tell the worker you have an immediate need for food or shelter.
2. If you are not eligible for regular assistance, ask to be assessed for hardship assistance and say which situation applies to you.
3. You must re-apply each month; hardship assistance is granted one month at a time.
4. If the category is repayable, you will sign a repayment agreement. Ask an advocate before you sign if you are unsure.
programs.name: BC Hardship Assistance
programs.phone_script: If you're turned down for income assistance but have no way to pay for food or rent, BC has hardship assistance, paid one month at a time and sometimes repayable, for example if you're waiting for EI or a pension. Call 1-866-866-0800 and say you have an immediate need. TAPS in Victoria can help you at 250-361-3521.

programs.amount: Rent is set at 30% of your gross household income (with a minimum rent). No cash is paid to you; the subsidy is the lower rent.
programs.eligibility_summary: You live in B.C., everyone in your household is a citizen, permanent resident, sponsored refugee or refugee claimant (not under sponsorship), your gross income is below the Housing Income Limit for your area, and you are a senior (55+), a person with a disability living independently, a family with a child, or a single person or couple who is homeless or at risk. For BC Housing-managed buildings, assets must be under $100,000.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Together Against Poverty Society (TAPS), 828 View Street, Victoria. Phone 250-361-3521.
Free tenant advocacy and help with housing forms.
For a housing outreach worker, call 211.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Apply to the Housing Registry online at bchousing.org, or by mail, fax or in person at a BC Housing office. One application covers many buildings.
2. Say on the form that you need an accessible or adapted unit, and describe what you need.
3. Include documents showing income and any health or safety urgency; you can be placed in a higher priority group.
4. Keep your contact details current; call Applicant Services at 1-800-257-7756 with any changes.
programs.name: BC Housing subsidized and accessible housing (Housing Registry)
programs.phone_script: BC Housing has a central wait list called the Housing Registry for apartments where rent is about thirty percent of your income. Seniors 55 and over, people with disabilities and people at risk of homelessness can apply, and you can ask for an accessible unit on the same form. The wait is long, so the sooner you apply the better; call 1-800-257-7756 to start.

programs.amount: Monthly support plus a shelter allowance. Single person: $560 support plus up to $500 shelter ($1,060 a month). Couple: $955 support plus up to $695 shelter. Single parent with one child: $710 support plus up to $695 shelter. Rate table effective August 1, 2023 (still posted 2026-09-01). Includes basic medical coverage and can unlock crisis supplements, bus passes and other help.
programs.eligibility_summary: BC residents who are out of work or not earning enough to meet basic needs, or who urgently need food, shelter or medical care, and who have used up other sources of income and assets. Most first-time applicants must look for work for three weeks first, unless they have a disability, are 65 or older, are fleeing abuse, or are a single parent of a child under 3.
programs.help_in_victoria: Together Against Poverty Society (TAPS), 828 View Street, Victoria. Phone 250-361-3521. TAPS gives free income assistance advocacy, including help with applications and appeals. Or dial 2-1-1.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Apply online at My Self Serve (myselfserve.gov.bc.ca), call 1-866-866-0800, or visit a local Ministry office.
2. Have ready: ID for you and your family, your Social Insurance Number, what you pay for rent and utilities, and your bank balance.
3. Most new applicants must do a three-week work search and record it on the Work Search Activities form. Exemptions apply.
4. If you are turned down, ask about hardship assistance and ask for a reconsideration.
programs.name: BC Income Assistance
programs.phone_script: BC Income Assistance is monthly money for people who can't cover basic needs; a single person can get $560 for support plus up to $500 for rent. You can apply online, by calling 1-866-866-0800, or at a ministry office. Most people have to look for work for three weeks first, unless they have a disability or are 65 or older.

programs.amount: Rebates of up to $20,000 per household (lifetime) for home changes like ramps, grab bars, walk-in showers and stair lifts.
programs.eligibility_summary: You or someone in your home has a permanent disability or lasting loss of ability, the home is your main residence in B.C., your household income before tax is under $146,270, your assets (not counting the home) are under $100,000, and the home's assessed value is under the program limit for your area. Homeowners apply alone; tenants apply together with their landlord.
programs.help_in_victoria: Call 211 for an occupational therapy or seniors' service that can help with the assessment and the forms.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Check the Maximum Rebate Schedule on bchousing.org to see what each adaptation pays.
2. Gather proof of status in Canada, the latest CRA Notice of Assessment for everyone 19+, bank statements, and proof of address.
3. Get a home assessment from an occupational therapist or other health professional if your adaptation needs one.
4. Apply before starting work. Homeowners use the homeowner application; tenants and landlords file a joint application.
5. Once approved in writing, you have 180 days to finish the work and send in receipts.
programs.name: BC Rebate for Accessible Home Adaptations (BC RAHA)
programs.phone_script: BC RAHA pays up to twenty thousand dollars toward changes to your home, like a ramp or a walk-in shower, if you have a permanent disability and a low or moderate income. You must apply and be approved before the work starts. Call BC Housing at 1-800-257-7756.

programs.amount: Seniors 65+: $3 single ride, $6 DayPASS, $45 concession 30-day pass (as listed September 2026). Attendants ride free with riders who use a wheelchair, scooter, handyDART or a CNIB pass. Children 12 and under ride free. Low-income seniors and people on disability assistance can get the annual BC Bus Pass for $45 a year (see the BC Bus Pass note). Check current amount.
programs.eligibility_summary: Seniors' fares are for people 65 and older with valid ID. A free attendant must get on and off at the same stop as you and help you. The BC Bus Pass needs a separate application through the province. All Victoria buses are low-floor or lift-equipped and kneel for easier boarding.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Victoria Regional Transit info: 250-382-6161.
handyDART office: 250-727-7811.
Victoria Disability Resource Centre, 250-595-0044, for help with the BC Bus Pass or handyDART registration.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. For a seniors' fare, just show ID when you board or load a concession pass on an Umo card or the Umo app.
2. For a free attendant, no application: the attendant boards with you at the same stop.
3. For the annual BC Bus Pass, apply through the province (see the bc-bus-pass note).
4. Questions: call Victoria Regional Transit at 250-382-6161 (Monday to Friday 6 am to 7 pm, Saturday 7 am to 7 pm, Sunday from 8 am). handyDART: 250-727-7811. Umo card help: 1-877-380-8181. Accessibility email: bctransitaccessibility@bctransit.com.
programs.name: BC Transit Victoria accessible and seniors fares
programs.phone_script: On Victoria buses, seniors 65 and up pay a lower fare, kids 12 and under ride free, and if you use a wheelchair, scooter, handyDART or a CNIB pass, one helper rides with you for free. If you're on a low income, ask about the $45-a-year BC Bus Pass. For questions call BC Transit at 250-382-6161.

programs.amount: This credit has ended. The April 2025 payment was the last one. In its final year (July 2024 to June 2025) it paid up to $504 per adult, $252 for a spouse or first child of a single parent, and $126 for each other child. People who never filed 2023 or earlier tax returns can still claim past payments by filing those returns.
programs.eligibility_summary: No new payments. If you were a BC resident with low or modest income in 2023 or an earlier year and did not file a tax return for that year, filing it now can still get you the credit for that year. The CRA works it out automatically.
programs.help_in_victoria: Free tax clinics can file past-year returns (see the cvitp note). Dial 2-1-1 for a clinic near you.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. There is nothing to apply for going forward; the credit ended with the April 2025 payment.
2. If you missed filing a tax return for 2023 or an earlier year, file it now. The CRA will calculate and pay any credit you were owed for that year.
3. Questions: CRA at 1-800-387-1193.
programs.name: BC Climate Action Tax Credit (ended April 2025)
programs.phone_script: The BC Climate Action Tax Credit has ended; the last payment was April 2025. If you never filed taxes for 2023 or earlier, filing those returns now can still get you the credit for those years. For ongoing help with costs, ask me about the Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit.

programs.amount: Up to $1,750 a year for the first child, $1,100 for the second, and $900 for each additional child, plus up to $500 a year for low-income single parents (July 2026 to June 2027, based on 2025 income). Paid monthly with the Canada Child Benefit.
programs.eligibility_summary: BC families with children under 18 who get the Canada Child Benefit. Families with 2025 income under $30,176 get the full amount. Families between $30,176 and $96,562 get a reduced amount with a guaranteed minimum. Above $96,562 it is reduced further.
programs.help_in_victoria: Dial 2-1-1 for a free tax clinic or family resource centre near you. See the cvitp note for free tax filing.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Apply for the Canada Child Benefit (CCB) with the Canada Revenue Agency. If your child is already registered for the CCB, you are automatically registered for the BC Family Benefit. No extra form.
2. File your tax return every year, and so must your spouse or partner.
3. Questions: CRA at 1-800-387-1193.
programs.name: BC Family Benefit
programs.phone_script: The BC Family Benefit is a monthly payment for BC families with children under 18, and right now the full amount is $1,750 a year for a first child. It comes automatically with the Canada Child Benefit, so the main thing is to apply for the Canada Child Benefit and file your taxes every year. The CRA number is 1-800-387-1193.

programs.amount: Non-medical help at home for seniors: light housekeeping, grocery shopping, rides to appointments, friendly visits, yard work, minor repairs, snow shovelling. Some services are free; others charge a fee on a sliding scale based on income.
programs.eligibility_summary: You are a senior (the Victoria program has described its clients as 65 and older; confirm when you call) living in Victoria or Oak Bay and want help with everyday non-medical tasks so you can stay at home. You register with one of three partner agencies: James Bay Community Project, Capital City Volunteers, or Oak Bay Volunteer Services. Fees depend on income; low-income seniors pay little or nothing.
programs.help_in_victoria:
James Bay Community Project, Better at Home coordinator: 250-388-7844 ext. 334, betterathome@jbcp.bc.ca.
Capital City Volunteers also delivers the program (same coordinator number).
For other municipalities: betterathome.ca, or see 211 (dial 2-1-1).
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Call the Victoria and Oak Bay Better at Home coordinator at James Bay Community Project: 250-388-7844, extension 334, or email betterathome@jbcp.bc.ca.
2. Say what you need help with and where you live; you will be registered with the partner agency for your area.
3. A short intake sets your fee on the sliding scale. Bring or state your income.
4. Services are scheduled by staff or trained volunteers. Outside Victoria and Oak Bay, find the local program at betterathome.ca or call United Way BC at 604-268-1312.
programs.name: Better at Home (Victoria and Oak Bay)
programs.phone_script: Better at Home is a program for seniors that sends help with housekeeping, groceries, rides to appointments, and friendly visits so you can stay in your own home. Some services are free and the rest are on a sliding scale based on your income. In Victoria and Oak Bay call the coordinator at 250-388-7844, extension 334.

programs.amount: Free community centre services: an Income Assistance Outreach worker on site Thursdays, a free 15-minute phone legal clinic on Tuesdays, housing outreach, a family self-sufficiency program with free financial workshops, 55+ recreation, and a drop-off point for free TAPS tax filing.
programs.eligibility_summary: Anyone in Victoria, with a focus on the Burnside Gorge neighbourhood. No cost. The income assistance and legal appointments are by booking; the centre itself is drop-in.
programs.help_in_victoria:
BGCA: 250-388-5251, 471 Cecelia Road.
TAPS: 250-361-3521, 828 View Street.
Or call 211.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Call 250-388-5251 or email info@burnsidegorge.ca.
2. Visit 471 Cecelia Road, Victoria (V8T 4T4), Monday to Friday 8:30 am to 5 pm.
3. To see the Income Assistance Outreach worker (Thursdays 11 am to 2:45 pm) or the legal clinic (Tuesdays 2 to 3 pm), call to book.
4. For free tax filing, drop off your tax papers at the centre; a trained TAPS volunteer prepares and files your return.
programs.name: Burnside Gorge Community Association (BGCA)
programs.phone_script: Burnside Gorge Community Centre at 471 Cecelia Road has an income assistance worker on site on Thursdays, a free phone legal clinic on Tuesdays, and a drop-off for free tax filing. Call 250-388-5251 to book, Monday to Friday, 8:30 to 5.

programs.amount: Non-refundable credit for people who support a spouse, partner or relative with a mental or physical infirmity. For the 2025 tax year: $2,687 on line 30300, 30400 or 30500, and up to $8,601 on line 30425 or 30450. The $8,601 amount for an adult dependant on line 30450 shrinks as the dependant's net income rises and ends at $28,798 (2025).
programs.eligibility_summary: You support a spouse or common-law partner with a mental or physical infirmity, or a child, grandchild, parent, grandparent, brother, sister, aunt, uncle, niece or nephew (yours or your partner's) who depends on you for food, shelter or clothing because of an infirmity. Relatives other than children must have lived in Canada at some time in the year. The CRA may ask for a signed note from a medical practitioner saying when the infirmity began and how long it will last, unless the person already has an approved Disability Tax Credit.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Together Against Poverty Society (TAPS), 828 View Street, 250-361-3521: free, year-round income tax filing services (from tapsbc.ca).
CRA individual tax enquiries: 1-800-959-8281.
Or call 211 for caregiver support and tax clinics.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Confirm the person depends on you and has a lasting mental or physical infirmity.
2. Get a signed statement from a medical practitioner if there is no approved T2201 on file.
3. Fill in Schedule 5 to work out the amounts.
4. Enter the result on the right line: 30300 (spouse), 30400 (eligible dependant), 30425 (extra caregiver amount for spouse or eligible dependant 18+), 30450 (other infirm dependants 18+), or 30500 (infirm children under 18, no Schedule 5 needed).
5. Keep the documents; do not send them.
6. Special rules apply if you pay child support or share custody.
programs.name: Canada Caregiver Credit
programs.phone_script: The Canada caregiver credit lowers your income tax if you support a spouse, parent, child or other close relative with a lasting physical or mental condition. For 2025 the base amount is two thousand six hundred and eighty-seven dollars, with up to eight thousand six hundred and one dollars more depending on who you care for and their income. You claim it on Schedule 5 of your tax return, and the CRA may ask for a doctor's note.

programs.amount: A monthly rent top-up paid to you or your landlord. The amount depends on your rent and income; BC Housing does not publish a flat rate. Check current amount.
programs.eligibility_summary: People in BC who pay more than 30% of their gross monthly income on rent, have low income (annual limits posted by BC Housing: $31,992 for singles and couples without children, $40,000 for families of 4 or less, $44,400 for families of 5 or more), and belong to a priority group in need of housing. You cannot apply directly: BC Housing or a non-profit housing provider must select you.
programs.help_in_victoria: Together Against Poverty Society (TAPS), 828 View Street, Victoria. Phone 250-361-3521. TAPS helps with tenancy and income assistance problems. For a housing provider near you, dial 2-1-1.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. There is no direct application. BC Housing picks people from The Housing Registry, and non-profit housing providers pick people from the priority groups they serve.
2. Get on The Housing Registry (apply through BC Housing) so you can be selected.
3. If a provider invites you, fill in their application and give them ID, proof of income (pay stub), proof of rent, and your banking information.
4. The provider checks eligibility, sends an approval letter, and sets up direct deposit to you or your landlord.
programs.name: Canada-BC Housing Benefit (CBCHB)
programs.phone_script: The Canada-BC Housing Benefit is a monthly rent top-up for low-income renters who don't fit the other BC Housing programs. You can't apply directly; BC Housing or a non-profit housing provider has to pick you, so the first step is getting on The Housing Registry. BC Housing's number is 1-800-257-7756.

programs.amount: Up to $8,157 a year ($679.75 a month) per child under 6 and $6,883 a year ($573.58 a month) per child aged 6 to 17, for July 2026 to June 2027. Full amount if 2025 family net income is under $38,237. Plus up to $3,480 a year Child Disability Benefit per child who qualifies for the Disability Tax Credit.
programs.eligibility_summary: You live with a child under 18 and are mainly responsible for their care, you are a resident of Canada for tax purposes, and you or your spouse is a citizen, permanent resident, protected person, or eligible temporary resident. The amount goes down as family income rises above $38,237 (2025 income).
programs.help_in_victoria: Dial 2-1-1 for a free tax clinic or family resource centre near you. See the cvitp note for free help filing taxes.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Apply as soon as the child is born or comes to live with you. Many BC parents apply when they register the birth (Automated Benefits Application).
2. Or apply online in your CRA account, or mail form RC66 (Canada Child Benefits Application).
3. File your tax return every year, and so must your spouse or partner, or the payments stop.
4. Questions: CRA at 1-800-387-1193.
programs.name: Canada Child Benefit (CCB)
programs.phone_script: The Canada Child Benefit is a tax-free monthly payment for anyone raising a child under 18; this year it's up to $679.75 a month for a child under 6 and $573.58 for a child 6 to 17, depending on your family income. You apply through the Canada Revenue Agency, and you must file taxes every year to keep it. Their number is 1-800-387-1193.

programs.amount: Up to $204.20 a month for July 2026 to June 2027 (was $200 a month for July 2025 to June 2026). Income tested. Up to $10,210 of a single person's working income is ignored ($14,294 for a couple). A one-time $150 supplement to help with the cost of getting the DTC starts fall 2026.
programs.eligibility_summary: You must be 18 to 64, approved for the Disability Tax Credit, a resident of Canada for tax purposes, and a citizen, permanent resident, protected person, person registered under the Indian Act, or a temporary resident who has lived in Canada for the past 18 months. You and your spouse or partner must have filed your tax return for the previous year. The amount goes down as adjusted family net income goes up.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Victoria Disability Resource Centre, 817A Fort Street, 250-595-0044 — help applying for disability benefits.
Service Canada, CDB line: 1-833-486-3007.
Or call 211 for other options.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Get approved for the Disability Tax Credit first.
2. If Service Canada mailed you a letter with a 6-digit application code, apply online with that code and your SIN.
3. If you did not get a letter, apply online, by phone at 1-833-486-3007, in person at a Service Canada office, or by mailing the paper form to the CDB Processing Centre, P.O. Box 60, Boucherville QC J4B 5E6.
4. Give direct deposit details if you can.
5. A legal representative can apply for you with proof of their authority.
6. Payments start the month after approval, on the third Thursday, with back pay for up to 24 months (not before June 2025).
programs.name: Canada Disability Benefit (CDB)
programs.phone_script: The Canada Disability Benefit is a monthly federal payment of up to about two hundred dollars for people aged 18 to 64 who have the Disability Tax Credit and a low or modest income. You apply through Service Canada online, by phone at 1-833-486-3007, or at their office. If you do not have the Disability Tax Credit yet, that is the first step.

programs.amount: Pays for eligible dental care at plan fees. Family net income under $70,000: 100% of plan fees covered, no co-payment. $70,000 to $79,999: 60% covered, you pay 40%. $80,000 to $89,999: 40% covered, you pay 60%. Dentists may charge more than the plan fee; you pay any difference. Applications for the 2026-2027 benefit period are open.
programs.eligibility_summary: You must have no access to private dental insurance (through work, a pension, a family member's plan, a student plan, or a policy you bought), you and your spouse or partner must have filed last year's tax return, your adjusted family net income must be under $90,000, and you must be a Canadian resident for tax purposes. People with dental coverage through a government social program (for example BC disability assistance) can still qualify and the plans coordinate. You must confirm eligibility every year.
programs.help_in_victoria:
CDCP line (Service Canada): 1-833-537-4342, TTY 1-833-677-6262, or visit a Service Canada office.
Or call 211 for community dental clinics.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Check box 45 on your T4 or box 015 on your T4A: a code of 1 means no employer or pension dental coverage.
2. File your taxes (and your spouse's).
3. Apply online at canada.ca or by phone at 1-833-537-4342 (TTY 1-833-677-6262) with your SIN, date of birth, address and any spouse details.
4. Wait for your welcome letter and Sun Life member card.
5. Find a dentist, denturist or hygienist who takes CDCP patients and show your card. Some services need pre-approval.
6. Renew every year before the deadline (June 1 for the 2026-2027 period) to avoid a gap.
programs.name: Canadian Dental Care Plan (CDCP)
programs.phone_script: The Canadian Dental Care Plan pays for dental care if you have no private dental insurance and your family income is under ninety thousand dollars. If your income is under seventy thousand, it covers the full plan fee for eligible services. You need to have filed your taxes, and you can apply online or by calling 1-833-537-4342.

programs.amount: Tax-free payment every three months. For July 2026 to June 2027 (based on 2025 income): up to $679 a year for a single person, $890 for a couple, plus $234 for each child under 19. The benefit went up 25% in July 2026 and stays at that level until 2031.
programs.eligibility_summary: Residents of Canada aged 19 or older (or younger if you have a spouse or live with your child) with low or modest income. You can qualify even with no income. The CRA decides automatically when you file your tax return.
programs.help_in_victoria: Free tax clinics file returns for people with modest income (see the cvitp note). Dial 2-1-1 for a clinic near you.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. File your tax return every year, even with zero income. The CRA checks automatically.
2. New to Canada? Fill in form RC151 (GST/HST credit and CCB application for newcomers) instead for your first year.
3. Keep your address, marital status, and direct deposit details up to date with the CRA.
4. Questions: 1-800-387-1193.
programs.name: Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit (formerly the GST/HST credit)
programs.phone_script: The GST credit is now called the Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit: a tax-free payment every three months for people with low or modest income, up to $679 a year for a single person this year. There is no form; just file your taxes every year, even with no income, and the CRA sends it automatically. Their number is 1-800-387-1193.

programs.amount: Tax-free. Up to $3,480 a year ($290 a month) per eligible child for July 2026 to June 2027. Reduced once adjusted family net income passes $82,847 (by 3.2% of the excess for one child, 5.7% for two or more).
programs.eligibility_summary: You must already be eligible for the Canada Child Benefit for a child under 18, and that child must be approved for the Disability Tax Credit (Form T2201 certified by a medical practitioner and approved by the CRA). The amount depends on how many eligible children you have and your adjusted family net income from last year's tax return.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Victoria Disability Resource Centre, 817A Fort Street, 250-595-0044 — information and help with disability benefit applications.
CRA benefits line: 1-800-387-1193 (DTC questions: 1-800-959-8281).
Or call 211 for other options.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Apply for the Canada Child Benefit if you do not already get it.
2. Apply for the Disability Tax Credit for your child with Form T2201.
3. Once both are in place there is no separate application: the CRA adds the Child Disability Benefit to your monthly CCB automatically, including for the current and two previous benefit years.
4. For earlier years, write to your tax centre.
5. Keep filing your taxes every year (both parents), even with no income, or payments stop.
programs.name: Child Disability Benefit
programs.phone_script: The Child Disability Benefit is a tax-free monthly payment of up to two hundred and ninety dollars per child added to the Canada Child Benefit. To get it, your child needs to be approved for the Disability Tax Credit with Form T2201, and then the CRA adds it automatically. You can call the CRA at 1-800-387-1193 with questions.

programs.amount: No cash payment to you. CLBC funds services such as supported living, respite, employment support, skill development and homemaker help, based on an assessed plan.
programs.eligibility_summary: You are 19 or older and live in B.C., and either you have a developmental disability (significantly impaired intellectual and adaptive functioning that started before age 18), or, through the Personalized Supports Initiative, you have a diagnosis of Autism Spectrum Disorder or Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder and need a lot of help with daily tasks.
programs.help_in_victoria:
CLBC toll-free line 1-877-660-2522 will connect you to the Victoria area office.
For a local family support or self-advocacy group, call 211.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Call CLBC at 1-877-660-2522 or contact the local office to reach a facilitator.
2. The facilitator explains which assessments are needed and which approved professionals (such as a psychologist) can do them.
3. Send the completed assessments and CLBC eligibility forms to the facilitator.
4. CLBC confirms eligibility, then works with you on a support plan. You can start the process before you turn 19.
programs.name: Community Living BC (CLBC) supports
programs.phone_script: Community Living BC funds support services for adults 19 and over with a developmental disability, and for adults with autism or FASD who need a lot of help with daily life. It does not send you a cheque; it pays for things like support workers, respite and job help. Call 1-877-660-2522 and ask for a facilitator to check if you qualify.

programs.amount: Free legal help from a non-profit law firm for people in BC who cannot afford a lawyer: losing your housing, human rights complaints, mental health detentions, income and income-support benefit appeals, and workplace sexual harassment.
programs.eligibility_summary: People in BC with low or moderate incomes who have a legal problem in one of CLAS's areas: housing loss, a BC Human Rights Tribunal complaint, being held under the Mental Health Act, a denied or cut-off benefit (income assistance, PWD, CPP disability, EI, WorkSafeBC), or sexual harassment at work. Help is by phone from Vancouver, so Victoria residents can use it.
programs.help_in_victoria:
TAPS, 828 View Street, 250-361-3521, for income assistance and tenancy advocacy locally.
Access Pro Bono free legal advice: 1-877-762-6664.
CLAS by phone: 1-888-685-6222.
Or call 211.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Call 604-685-3425 or toll-free 1-888-685-6222.
2. Explain your problem. Intake staff decide if it fits one of their programs and whether you qualify financially.
3. If accepted, a CLAS lawyer or advocate advises you or represents you at the tribunal or review board.
4. If it is not a CLAS matter, they refer you to the right place.
programs.name: Community Legal Assistance Society (CLAS)
programs.phone_script: The Community Legal Assistance Society is a free non-profit law firm in BC. They help with losing your housing, human rights complaints, benefit appeals, and mental health detentions. Call them toll-free at 1-888-685-6222; most help is done by phone.

programs.amount: Depends on what you paid in. Maximum $1,507.65 a month at 65 (January 2026); the average new pension at 65 is $877.01 (April 2026). Taking it at 60 cuts it up to 36%; waiting to 70 adds up to 42%. Paid for life. Taxable.
programs.eligibility_summary: You are at least 60 and you made at least one valid contribution to the CPP, from work in Canada or from credits split with a former spouse after a separation. You can keep working while you get it. It is not automatic: you must apply.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Seniors Serving Seniors "Seniors Link" line: 250-413-3211, Monday to Thursday 9 am to 4 pm
(from sssbc.org).
Service Canada: 1-800-277-9914 (TTY 1-800-255-4786), or a Service Canada Centre in person.
For other local help with the form, see 211, or ask for a Reachable Benefits navigator.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Decide your start date. Standard age is 65. You can start any month from 60 to 70. You can apply up to 12 months ahead.
2. Check your Statement of Contributions and estimate in My Service Canada Account (MSCA) under "View my benefit estimates".
3. Apply online in MSCA: "Canada Pension Plan" section, then "Apply for Canada Pension Plan retirement pension". Decision by mail within about 28 days.
4. Or mail paper form ISP-1000 (Application for a Canada Pension Plan Retirement Pension). Decision within about 120 days.
5. On the form, fill in the child-rearing section (11A and 11B) if you stayed home with children under 7. Have your SIN and bank details ready.
6. If you already get CPP disability, it changes to a retirement pension automatically at 65; no application needed.
programs.name: Canada Pension Plan (CPP) retirement pension
programs.phone_script: The Canada Pension Plan retirement pension is a monthly payment based on what you paid in while working; you can start it any time between 60 and 70, and starting later means a bigger cheque for life. It does not start on its own, so you have to apply. Call Service Canada at 1-800-277-9914 or apply through My Service Canada Account.

programs.amount: Not a payment on its own. It removes low-earning years spent raising children under 7 from your CPP calculation, so your CPP retirement, disability or survivor pension can be higher; it can also help you qualify for CPP disability. Only applied if it raises your amount.
programs.eligibility_summary: You (or your spouse) got Family Allowance or qualified for the Canada Child Benefit for a child born after December 31, 1958, and you had low or no earnings because you were the main caregiver of a child under 7. Both parents can qualify for different periods. You must ask for it; Service Canada does not apply it on its own.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Seniors Serving Seniors "Seniors Link" line: 250-413-3211, Monday to Thursday 9 am to 4 pm
(from sssbc.org).
Service Canada: 1-800-277-9914 (TTY 1-800-255-4786).
For help gathering old documents (birth certificates, immigration records), see 211 or
ask for a Reachable Benefits navigator.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. When you apply for CPP retirement, fill in the child-rearing section (11A and 11B) of form ISP1000, or the same section online in My Service Canada Account. On the CPP disability form (ISP1151) there is also a section.
2. For other CPP benefits, or if you already get CPP, send form ISP1640 (Child Rearing Provision) or request it through My Service Canada Account.
3. For each child give the name, date of birth and SIN (or proof of birth if no SIN), plus proof of entry into Canada for a child born abroad.
4. List any months you were not the primary caregiver or did not get Family Allowance or Canada Child Benefit.
programs.name: CPP child-rearing provisions
programs.phone_script: If you stayed home or worked less to raise a child under 7, the CPP child-rearing provision can take those low-income years out of your pension calculation so your CPP is higher. You have to ask for it, on the CPP application or with form ISP1640 if you already get CPP. Call Service Canada at 1-800-277-9914 and say you want to apply the child-rearing provision.

programs.amount: Monthly, taxable. 2026 maximum $1,741.20 a month; basic flat portion $610.46 plus an amount based on your CPP contributions. Average for new recipients $1,234.68 a month (canada.ca dates this figure to late 2025 or early 2026). Paid until age 65, then it becomes a CPP retirement pension.
programs.eligibility_summary: You must be over 18 and under 65, have a mental or physical disability that regularly stops you from doing any substantially gainful work, expect it to last indefinitely or to result in death, and have paid enough into CPP: contributions in at least 4 of the last 6 years, or at least 25 years of contributions including 3 of the last 6. Years spent raising children under 7, a past divorce, or work abroad may help you qualify. If you stopped working long ago you may still qualify if you have been continuously disabled since then.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Victoria Disability Resource Centre, 817A Fort Street, 250-595-0044 — help applying for disability benefits.
Service Canada CPP line: 1-800-277-9914 (TTY 1-800-255-4786).
Or call 211 for other options.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Apply as soon as your disability becomes severe and prolonged; do not wait.
2. Apply online through My Service Canada Account (MSCA), or by mail with the paper application.
3. Print, sign and upload the consent form ISP-2502.
4. After you apply, have your doctor or nurse practitioner complete the Medical Report (ISP-2519), or the Terminal Illness Medical Attestation (ISP-2530B) if you have a terminal illness; fill in sections 1 and 2 yourself first.
5. If you already get disability payments from an insurer or BC, ask them to send Service Canada your latest medical reports instead.
6. Service Canada aims to decide within 120 days; terminal and grave conditions are handled faster.
7. If refused, you can ask for a reconsideration.
programs.name: Canada Pension Plan Disability Benefit (CPP-D)
programs.phone_script: CPP disability is a monthly payment for people under 65 who paid into the Canada Pension Plan while working and now cannot work because of a long-term disability. In 2026 it pays up to about seventeen hundred dollars a month depending on your contributions. You apply through Service Canada, and your doctor fills in a medical report; you can call 1-800-277-9914 to start.

programs.amount: One-time payment of $2,500. For deaths on or after January 1, 2025 there is an extra $2,500 top-up (total $5,000) if the person never received CPP retirement or disability benefits and leaves no spouse or partner eligible for a survivor's pension.
programs.eligibility_summary: The person who died paid into the CPP for at least one-third of the years they could have (and no fewer than 3 years), or for at least 10 years. The estate applies first, within 60 days. If there is no estate or the executor does not apply, it can go to whoever paid the funeral, then the surviving spouse or partner, then next of kin.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Seniors Serving Seniors "Seniors Link" line: 250-413-3211, Monday to Thursday 9 am to 4 pm
(from sssbc.org).
Service Canada: 1-800-277-9914 (TTY 1-800-255-4786).
For grief support and help with paperwork after a death, see 211, or ask for a Reachable
Benefits navigator.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. The executor or estate administrator applies, ideally within 60 days of the death.
2. If there is no will or estate, the person who paid the funeral, the surviving spouse or partner, or next of kin can apply, in that order.
3. Online: sign in to My Service Canada Account and complete the CPP Death Benefit form.
4. Paper: form ISP1200 (Application for a Canada Pension Plan Death Benefit). Put the deceased's SIN and your own on every document. Mail it to Service Canada.
5. Payment takes about 6 to 12 weeks. The benefit is taxable to whoever receives it (the estate or the person).
programs.name: CPP death benefit
programs.phone_script: The CPP death benefit is a one-time payment of $2,500 when someone who paid into the Canada Pension Plan dies; since 2025 it can be $5,000 if the person never collected CPP and leaves no spouse. The executor applies first, or whoever paid the funeral. Call Service Canada at 1-800-277-9914; the paper form is ISP1200.

programs.amount: A small extra monthly CPP amount for each year you work and pay in while getting CPP. Maximum new PRB at 65: $54.69 a month (2026); average $25.76. Each year's PRB is added to your CPP for life.
programs.eligibility_summary: You are 60 to 70, you already get a CPP or QPP retirement pension, and you are working and paying CPP contributions. Under 65 the contributions are required; from 65 to 70 you can choose to stop with form CPT30. Contributions end at 70 no matter what. No application is needed; Service Canada pays it automatically the year after you contribute.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Seniors Serving Seniors "Seniors Link" line: 250-413-3211, Monday to Thursday 9 am to 4 pm
(from sssbc.org).
Service Canada: 1-800-277-9914 (TTY 1-800-255-4786). For the CPT30 form: Canada Revenue
Agency 1-800-959-8281.
For tax help, see 211 for a free tax clinic.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Nothing to apply for. If you work while getting CPP and contributions come off your pay (or you pay them as self-employed on Schedule 8), the PRB is set up automatically.
2. It starts the year after the contributions were made and is paid for life.
3. To stop contributing at 65 to 69, fill in CRA form CPT30, give a copy to each employer and send the original to the CRA. You can change your mind once per calendar year.
4. Self-employed: use Schedule 8 on your tax return to contribute or to stop.
programs.name: CPP Post-Retirement Benefit (PRB)
programs.phone_script: If you keep working after you start your CPP pension and CPP is still taken off your pay, you get a small extra pension for life for every year you contribute; you do not need to apply. From 65 to 69 you can choose to stop paying in by filing form CPT30 with the Canada Revenue Agency. For questions, call Service Canada at 1-800-277-9914.

programs.amount: Monthly for life. If you are 65 or older: 60% of what your late spouse's CPP would have been, up to $904.59 a month (2026). Under 65: a flat amount plus 37.5% of their pension, up to $803.54 a month (2026). Less if you already get your own CPP. Taxable.
programs.eligibility_summary: You were the legal spouse or the common-law partner (lived together at least one year) of someone who paid into the CPP and has died. A separated spouse can qualify if the person had no common-law partner. Any age; there is no income test. Your pension continues if you remarry. You must apply.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Seniors Serving Seniors "Seniors Link" line: 250-413-3211, Monday to Thursday 9 am to 4 pm
(from sssbc.org).
Service Canada: 1-800-277-9914 (TTY 1-800-255-4786).
For grief support and help with forms, see 211, or ask for a Reachable Benefits navigator.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Apply as soon as possible after the death. Back pay is limited to 12 months.
2. Online: sign in to My Service Canada Account and complete the CPP Survivor's Pension form; upload documents if you have them.
3. Paper: form ISP1300 (CPP survivor's pension and children's benefits). Write both your SIN and the deceased's SIN on every page. Mail it to Service Canada.
4. First payment takes about 6 to 12 weeks. It starts, at the earliest, the month after the death.
5. Apply for the CPP death benefit (one-time) and children's benefits at the same time if they apply.
programs.name: CPP survivor's pension
programs.phone_script: If your husband, wife or common-law partner paid into the Canada Pension Plan and has died, you can get a monthly survivor's pension for the rest of your life, at any age. You have to apply, and back pay only goes 12 months, so apply soon. Call Service Canada at 1-800-277-9914 and ask for the CPP survivor's pension; the form is ISP1300.

programs.amount: Free tax return preparation by trained volunteers. Filing a return is what triggers the GST/HST credit, BC climate action tax credit, GIS renewal, Canada Disability Benefit, rent help and many other payments. In Victoria, TAPS files taxes free all year; other clinics run mainly February to April.
programs.eligibility_summary: You need a modest income and a simple tax situation. Modest means total family income of about $40,000 for one person, $55,000 for two, $60,000 for three, $65,000 for four, $70,000 for five, plus $5,000 for each extra person. Simple means income from a job, pension, CPP, OAS, EI, disability or social assistance, RRSPs, scholarships or small interest. Clinics cannot do self-employment, business or rental income, capital gains, foreign income, bankruptcies or returns for someone who has died.
programs.help_in_victoria:
TAPS: 828 View Street, 250-361-3521 (year-round).
Burnside Gorge Community Centre: 471 Cecelia Road, 250-388-5251 (drop-off).
James Bay Community Project: 547 Michigan Street, 250-388-7844.
Disability Alliance BC Tax AID (income under $35,000, by phone): 1-877-940-7797.
CRA: 1-800-959-8281.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Year-round in Victoria: drop in at TAPS, 828 View Street, Monday, Tuesday, Thursday or Friday, 9 am to noon or 1 pm to 4 pm (250-361-3521). No appointment. Burnside Gorge Community Centre (471 Cecelia Road, 250-388-5251) takes drop-offs for TAPS. James Bay Community Project (250-388-7844) also runs a tax clinic.
2. Tax season (February to April): search the CRA clinic directory at canada.ca/taxes-help for walk-in, drop-off, appointment or virtual clinics near you.
3. Bring your SIN, ID, all tax slips (T4, T4A, T4A(P), T4A(OAS), T5007, T5), rent or property tax amounts, and last year's Notice of Assessment if you have it.
4. If a slip is missing, call the CRA at 1-800-959-8281.
programs.name: Free tax clinics in Victoria (CRA Community Volunteer Income Tax Program)
programs.phone_script: If your income is modest, volunteers will do your taxes for free, and filing is what unlocks benefits like GIS and the GST credit. In Victoria, TAPS at 828 View Street files taxes all year; just drop in Monday, Tuesday, Thursday or Friday, 9 to noon or 1 to 4. Bring your ID, your SIN and any tax slips.

programs.amount: Refundable (paid even if you owe no tax). For the 2025 tax year the disability supplement is up to $843, on top of a basic CWB of up to $1,633 for a single person or $2,813 for a family. The supplement shrinks once net income passes $37,740 (single) or $49,389 (family) and ends at $43,360 (single), $55,009 (family, one partner with DTC) or $60,629 (both partners with DTC). Half is paid in advance in July, October and January.
programs.eligibility_summary: You have working income from a job or self-employment, live in Canada all year, are 19 or older (or live with a spouse or child), and your net income is under the cut-off for BC. For the disability supplement you must also have an approved Disability Tax Credit (Form T2201) on file with the CRA. Full-time students for more than 13 weeks (without a dependant) and people in prison 90 days or more do not qualify.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Together Against Poverty Society (TAPS), 828 View Street, 250-361-3521 — free, year-round income tax filing services (tapsbc.ca).
CRA individual tax enquiries: 1-800-959-8281.
Or call 211 for free tax clinics.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Get the Disability Tax Credit approved.
2. File your tax return every year and claim the CWB on line 45300 using Schedule 6; tax software does this automatically.
3. Tick the disability supplement part of Schedule
6.
4. Advance payments of up to 50% are sent automatically in July, October and January based on last year's return.
5. If you are part of a couple where both have the DTC, each partner gets their own supplement.
programs.name: Canada Workers Benefit disability supplement
programs.phone_script: The Canada Workers Benefit is money back at tax time for people who work and earn a low income. If you also have the Disability Tax Credit, you get an extra disability supplement of up to eight hundred and forty-three dollars for 2025. You just need to file your tax return and fill in Schedule 6; part of it is paid in advance during the year.

programs.amount: Free. Advocates help you apply for the BC PWD designation and other disability benefits (Advocacy Access), help with the Disability Tax Credit and RDSP (Access DTC / Access RDSP), file taxes for people with income under $35,000 (Tax AID), and give free legal advice through the Disability Law Clinic.
programs.eligibility_summary: Any person with a disability in BC. Most help is by phone or video, so you do not need to be in Vancouver. There is no cost. The Tax AID service is for people with disabilities whose income is under $35,000. The office is open by appointment only.
programs.help_in_victoria:
For in-person help in Victoria, the Victoria Disability Resource Centre (817A Fort Street, 250-595-0044) and TAPS (828 View Street, 250-361-3521) do similar advocacy work locally.
DABC by phone: 1-800-663-1278.
Or call 211.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Call the toll-free line 1-800-663-1278 (Vancouver 604-875-0188), Monday to Friday 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.
2. Say what you need: PWD or income assistance help (Advocacy Access, 604-872-1278), Disability Tax Credit or RDSP help (Access DTC, 604-923-8136), tax filing (Tax AID, 236-477-1717 or 1-877-940-7797), or legal advice (Disability Law Clinic, 236-427-1108).
3. An advocate books a phone, video or in-person appointment. In-person is at #1450-605 Robson Street, Vancouver, by appointment only.
4. Have your BC Services Card or other ID, your income details and any letters from the ministry or the CRA ready.
programs.name: Disability Alliance BC (DABC)
programs.phone_script: Disability Alliance BC is a free province-wide service that helps people apply for disability benefits, the Disability Tax Credit and the RDSP. You can call them toll-free at 1-800-663-1278, Monday to Friday, 8:30 to 4:30. Most of their help is by phone, so you don't need to travel to Vancouver.

programs.amount: A deduction from income (line 21500) for the cost of supports you needed in order to work, go to school, or do grant-funded research: attendant care, sign-language or reading services, job coaching, assistive devices and software, service animals, tutoring and more. No fixed dollar cap; limited by the eligible expenses you paid that year (check current amount on Form T929).
programs.eligibility_summary: Only the person with the impairment in physical or mental functions can claim it. You must have paid for the supports so you could work, attend school, or do research under a grant. Many items need a prescription or a written certification from a medical practitioner. You cannot claim amounts that were reimbursed or that anyone claimed as medical expenses.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Together Against Poverty Society (TAPS), 828 View Street, 250-361-3521 — free, year-round income tax filing services (tapsbc.ca).
CRA individual tax enquiries: 1-800-959-8281.
Or call 211 for other options.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Keep receipts and any prescriptions or medical certifications for each support.
2. Fill in Form T929, Disability Supports Deduction, to calculate the amount.
3. Enter the result from line 12 of T929 on line 21500 of your tax return.
4. Do not attach the form or receipts; keep them in case the CRA asks.
5. Claim in the year you paid; unused amounts cannot be carried to another year.
6. The CRA allows the same expense to be claimed on line 21500 or as a medical expense (line 33099), or split between the two, but never twice. A free tax clinic can help you compare.
programs.name: Disability Supports Deduction
programs.phone_script: The disability supports deduction lets you subtract from your income the cost of things you needed to work or study because of a disability, like attendant care, interpreters, tutoring or special software. You work it out on Form T929 and put it on line 21500 of your tax return. TAPS in Victoria at 250-361-3521 offers free income tax filing help.

programs.amount: Non-refundable credit. For the 2025 tax year the disability amount is $10,138 (plus a $5,914 supplement if under 18). It lowers income tax owed; the tax saving is a percentage of that amount, so check current amount for your case. Can be claimed back up to 10 years. Opens the door to the CDB, RDSP, Child Disability Benefit and CWB disability supplement.
programs.eligibility_summary: You may qualify if a medical practitioner certifies that you have a severe and prolonged impairment. That means a marked restriction in one category (walking, mental functions, dressing, feeding, eliminating, hearing, speaking, vision), or significant limitations in two or more categories together, or you need life-sustaining therapy. There is no income test and no age limit. Children qualify too.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Victoria Disability Resource Centre, 817A Fort Street, 250-595-0044 — information, referral and help applying for disability benefits.
Together Against Poverty Society (TAPS), 828 View Street, 250-361-3521 — free, year-round income tax filing services (tapsbc.ca).
CRA DTC line: 1-800-959-8281.
Or call 211 for other options.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Find a medical practitioner who can certify your impairment (doctor or nurse practitioner for any impairment; optometrist, audiologist, occupational therapist, physiotherapist, psychologist or speech-language pathologist for specific ones).
2. Fill out Part A of Form T2201 yourself, online through CRA My Account or by phone, or on the paper form.
3. Your practitioner fills out Part B (both parts must use the same method, digital or paper).
4. Digital forms go to the CRA automatically; paper forms are mailed to a tax centre (Jonquiere, Sudbury or Winnipeg). Do not upload paper forms through the CRA account.
5. If approved, claim the disability amount on line 31600 of your tax return. Tick the box on the form asking the CRA to adjust past returns, or ask in writing.
programs.name: Disability Tax Credit (DTC)
programs.phone_script: The Disability Tax Credit is a tax credit for people with a serious long-term impairment. Your doctor fills in part of a form called T2201, and once approved it lowers your taxes and unlocks other benefits like the Canada Disability Benefit. You can call the CRA at 1-800-959-8281 or the Victoria Disability Resource Centre at 250-595-0044 for help applying.

programs.amount: Paid weekly for up to 26 weeks: 55% of your average insurable earnings, up to a maximum of $729 a week (figure shown on canada.ca as of 2026-09-01; the maximum changes each January, so check current amount). Some employers add a top-up. Families with income of $25,921 or less may get a family supplement.
programs.eligibility_summary: You cannot work for medical reasons (illness, injury, quarantine or another medical condition), your usual weekly earnings have dropped by more than 40% for at least one week, and you worked 600 insurable hours in the last 52 weeks or since your last claim. You need a medical certificate from a doctor, nurse practitioner or other listed professional saying you cannot work and for roughly how long. You must otherwise be available for work if not for your condition. Use employer-paid sick leave first if you have it.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Service Canada EI line: 1-800-206-7218, or visit a Service Canada office in person.
Or call 211 for local employment and advocacy services.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Apply online at canada.ca as soon as you stop working; waiting more than 4 weeks can cost you benefits. Do not wait for documents.
2. Have your SIN, mailing address, banking details and employer information ready.
3. Get a medical certificate signed by your treating practitioner (Service Canada form or their own letterhead with start date and expected length).
4. Your employer sends a Record of Employment; check it was sent.
5. Upload the medical certificate in My Service Canada Account if asked, or keep it for 6 years.
6. A benefit statement with an access code arrives by mail; use it to track your claim.
7. Questions: 1-800-206-7218.
programs.name: Employment Insurance sickness benefits
programs.phone_script: EI sickness benefits pay fifty-five percent of your earnings, up to a weekly maximum, for up to 26 weeks when you cannot work because you are sick or injured. You need six hundred hours of work in the past year and a note from your doctor. Apply online right away, because waiting more than four weeks can cost you money, and you can call Service Canada at 1-800-206-7218.

programs.amount: BC Hydro Customer Crisis Fund: a one-time grant of up to $800 (electric heat) or $700 (other heat) applied to an overdue bill, once per account holder per year. Free Energy Saving Kit (LED bulbs, showerhead, weather stripping and more) for income-qualified homes, one per five years. Energy Conservation Assistance Program: a free home energy visit and free upgrades, which can include insulation and a heat pump. Income limit for the kit and ECAP: $51,100 for one person, $63,600 for two (previous year's household income, figures on the 2026 pages).
programs.eligibility_summary: Customer Crisis Fund: you hold a residential BC Hydro account for your main home, you are at least 21 days overdue or facing disconnection, you owe $1,000 or less and have tried to pay, and a life event in the last 12 months (job or benefit loss, medical costs, a death) caused a temporary crisis. Energy Saving Kit and ECAP (BC Hydro or FortisBC): your household's combined income last year was under the limit for your household size ($51,100 for one person, $63,600 for two, $78,200 for three, $94,900 for four); renters qualify if the utility account is in their name. A GIS, SAFER or disability assistance letter is accepted as proof of income.
programs.help_in_victoria:
BC Hydro: 1-800-224-9376. FortisBC gas: 1-888-224-2710.
BC Hydro tells Crisis Fund applicants with general questions to call 211. See 211 (dial 2-1-1) for local emergency utility help.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Behind on a BC Hydro bill: first call 1-800-224-9376 (1-800-BCHYDRO) to set up a catch-up payment plan or deferral. Then apply for the Customer Crisis Fund online at app.bchydro.com/ccf-application or on the paper form at a Service BC office; decisions take about 21 days.
2. Free Energy Saving Kit: apply online at bchydro.com (savings based on income) or call 1-800-224-9376 with your account number; allow three to six weeks. FortisBC gas customers: fortisbc.com, income-qualified offers, or 1-888-224-2710.
3. Energy Conservation Assistance Program (free home visit and upgrades): apply through BC Hydro or FortisBC with proof of income for everyone 18 and over (Notice of Assessment, or a benefit letter such as GIS, SAFER or disability assistance). Renters need a landlord consent form. Program outreach line (CLEAResult, for BC Hydro): 1-888-798-7658.
4. Fortis electricity customers (not Victoria) call 1-866-436-7847.
programs.name: BC Hydro and FortisBC low-income programs (Customer Crisis Fund, free Energy Saving Kit, Energy Conservation Assistance Program)
programs.phone_script: If you're behind on your BC Hydro bill because of a job loss, illness or a death in the family, BC Hydro has a Customer Crisis Fund that can pay up to eight hundred dollars of the overdue amount, and you don't pay it back. If your income is modest, you can also get a free energy-saving kit and a free home visit with free upgrades. Start by calling 1-800-224-9376.

programs.amount: Fair PharmaCare: no deductible if family net income is $30,000 or less, then PharmaCare pays 70% of eligible drug costs (75% if someone in the family was born before 1940) up to a yearly maximum. Plan C: 100% of eligible drugs for people on income or disability assistance. Plan G: 100% of many psychiatric medications for one year at a time.
programs.eligibility_summary: Any B.C. resident with MSP can register for Fair PharmaCare; help is based on your family net income from two years ago. Plan C is automatic if you receive income assistance, disability assistance, hardship assistance or Medical Services Only. Plan G is for people with a mental health condition who cannot afford their psychiatric medication; a prescriber applies for you.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Your pharmacist can check which plan you are on and often register you for Fair PharmaCare on the spot.
Call 211 for a local seniors' or mental-health service that helps with forms.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Fair PharmaCare: register online at my.gov.bc.ca/ahdc or call 1-800-663-7100. Registration is free and you only do it once.
2. Plan C: nothing to do; the ministry enrols you when you get assistance.
3. Plan G: ask your doctor, nurse practitioner or psychiatrist. They complete form HLTH 3497, you sign it, and they fax it to a Mental Health and Substance Use centre. Renew every year.
programs.name: Fair PharmaCare (with Plan C and Plan G)
programs.phone_script: PharmaCare helps pay for prescriptions, and if your family income is thirty thousand dollars or less, Fair PharmaCare has no deductible, but you must register once at 1-800-663-7100. If you are on income or disability assistance you are already fully covered by Plan C. If you take psychiatric medication and cannot afford it, ask your doctor about Plan G.

programs.amount: Up to $1,123.17 a month if you are single, widowed or divorced; up to $676.09 a month each if your spouse also gets full OAS (July to September 2026 rates). Tax-free. Paid on top of OAS.
programs.eligibility_summary: You are 65 or older, you get the Old Age Security pension, you live in Canada, and your income is low. For July 2026 to June 2027 that means under $22,800 a year if you are single (not counting OAS), or a combined income under $30,096 if your spouse gets full OAS, under $42,144 if your spouse gets the Allowance, or under $54,624 if your spouse gets neither. You cannot get it while you are under a sponsorship agreement.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Seniors Serving Seniors "Seniors Link" line: 250-413-3211, weekdays 9 am to 4 pm
(from sssbc.org).
Service Canada: 1-800-277-9914 (TTY 1-800-255-4786).
Free tax clinics (CRA Community Volunteer Income Tax Program) help low-income seniors
file the return that keeps GIS going; see 211 for the nearest clinic.
Reachable Benefits navigators can check the letter you got and help you apply.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. If you get an automatic OAS enrolment letter near age 64, it will say whether Service Canada will also enrol you in GIS automatically.
2. If the letter invites you to apply, or you already get OAS but never applied for GIS, apply: sign in to My Service Canada Account and choose "Apply for Old Age Security and manage my benefits", or mail paper form ISP-3025 (GIS only) or ISP-3550 (OAS and GIS together).
3. Have your SIN, your spouse's SIN and date of birth, where you have lived since 18, and your bank details.
4. File your tax return every year by April 30. GIS is recalculated every July from last year's return. If you do not file, it stops.
5. If your income dropped (retired, pension ended), tell Service Canada. They can use this year's estimated income instead of last year's.
programs.name: Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS)
programs.phone_script: The Guaranteed Income Supplement is a tax-free monthly payment added to Old Age Security for seniors with low income; a single person can get up to about $1,123 a month on top of OAS. You qualify if you are 65 or over, get OAS, and your income apart from OAS is under $22,800 for a single person or higher limits for couples.
