To check or apply, call Service Canada at 1-800-277-9914, and make sure you file a tax return every year.

programs.amount: Free library services for people who find print hard to use: large print, audiobooks, ebooks, the CELA and NNELS accessible collections, DAISY audiobook players (Victor Readers) to borrow, and staff help at any branch. Home delivery for people who cannot get to a branch: check current details.
programs.eligibility_summary: Anyone with a Greater Victoria library card who has a print disability (low vision, blindness, a learning or physical disability that makes reading print hard). Registration is by self-identification; you do not need a doctor's note. A library card is free for residents.
programs.help_in_victoria:
GVPL customer service: 250-940-4875.
Better at Home Victoria (rides and friendly visits) can help someone get to a branch.
Or call 211.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Call customer service at 250-940-4875 (staff available Monday to Saturday, 10 am to 6 pm) or ask at any branch.
2. Say you have a print disability. You will be registered for accessible services; no paperwork from a doctor is needed.
3. Ask about borrowing a Victor Reader, joining CELA or NNELS, and about delivery if you cannot travel to a branch.
4. Main branch: 735 Broughton Street, Victoria (V8W 3H2).
programs.name: Greater Victoria Public Library accessible services
programs.phone_script: The Greater Victoria Public Library has free services for people who find print hard to read: large print, audiobooks, and players you can borrow. You just tell them you need it; no doctor's note. Call 250-940-4875 or ask at any branch, and ask about delivery if you can't get out.

programs.amount: handyDART rides cost the same as a regular BC Transit bus fare (ask BC Transit whether your BC Bus Pass is accepted). Taxi Saver: one $80 package of taxi coupons per month for $40 (50% off).
programs.eligibility_summary: handyDART is door-to-door transit in Greater Victoria for people whose disability makes it hard to use regular buses. You must register first. Taxi Saver is for permanently registered handyDART riders aged 12 or older who hold a handyPASS.
programs.help_in_victoria:
BC Transit Victoria handyDART office: bookings and questions 250-727-7811 (press 0).
Taxi Saver Program: 250-995-5618, taxisaver@bctransit.com.
For help filling in the form, call 211.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Fill in the Victoria handyDART Application Form (PDF on bctransit.com/victoria); you can add the optional Medical Verification of Eligibility form.
2. Once registered, book rides at 250-727-7811 and press 0. You can book up to 14 days ahead.
3. For Taxi Saver, mail your handyPASS number, return address and a $40 cheque payable to BC Transit to Taxi Saver Program, 520 Gorge Road East, PO Box 9861, Victoria BC V8W 9T5, or call 250-995-5618.
programs.name: HandyDART and Taxi Saver (Victoria)
programs.phone_script: handyDART is the door-to-door bus for people who cannot use a regular bus. You register once with a form from BC Transit, then call 250-727-7811 to book rides for the price of a normal bus fare. Once you are registered you can also buy Taxi Saver coupons at half price for trips handyDART cannot do.

programs.amount: Non-refundable credit on up to $20,000 a year of renovation costs that make a home safer or easier to get around in (2025 tax year). Worth about 14.5% of the costs for 2025 (up to about $2,900) and 14% from 2026 (up to $2,800), because the credit uses the lowest federal tax rate. One $20,000 limit per home per year. For 2025 the same cost can also be claimed as a medical expense.
programs.eligibility_summary: The work must be for a qualifying individual: someone 65 or older at the end of the year, or someone eligible for the Disability Tax Credit at any time in the year. The claim can be made by that person or by a relative who supports them (spouse, parent, grandparent, child, grandchild, sibling, aunt, uncle, niece or nephew who claimed, or could have claimed, a dependant or caregiver amount for them, or who can claim their disability amount). The work must be a lasting change to the person's main home in Canada that improves access, mobility or safety (ramp, walk-in shower, grab bars, stair lift, wider doors). Keep receipts.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Together Against Poverty Society (TAPS), 828 View Street, 250-361-3521: free year-round
tax filing and advocacy for people with disabilities on low incomes (from tapsbc.ca).
Seniors Serving Seniors "Seniors Link" line: 250-413-3211, weekdays 9 am to 4 pm
(from sssbc.org), for local home-adaptation and renovation referrals.
Canada Revenue Agency: 1-800-959-8281 (TTY 1-800-665-0354).
Free tax clinics (CRA Community Volunteer Income Tax Program); see 211.
BC also has separate home-adaptation help for renters and low-income owners; see the
BC housing notes in this knowledge base.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Do the renovation and keep every invoice and proof of payment showing the contractor's name, business address and GST/HST number, what was done, where and when.
2. When you file your tax return, complete the line 31285 chart on the Federal Worksheet and enter the result on line 31285.
3. Do not send receipts with the return; keep them in case the CRA asks.
4. If the same cost is also a medical expense, the CRA page for the 2025 tax year lets you claim it under both (lines 33099/33199).
5. The claim can be shared between the senior or disabled person and the relative who paid, up to $20,000 total per home.
programs.name: Home Accessibility Tax Credit (HATC, line 31285)
programs.phone_script: If you or someone in your home is 65 or over, or has the Disability Tax Credit, the Home Accessibility Tax Credit lets you claim up to $20,000 a year of lasting changes like a ramp, grab bars or a walk-in shower on your tax return, worth roughly $2,800 to $2,900 off your tax. Keep every receipt with the contractor's name and GST number. You or the family member who paid claims it on line 31285 when you file.

programs.amount: Publicly subsidized care at home or in a care home. What you pay depends on income. Home support is free for people on GIS, the Allowance, income/disability assistance, or War Veterans Allowance; otherwise a daily rate based on income. Adult day programs: up to $10 a day. Assisted living: 70% of after-tax income, minimum $1,253.80 a month (single, 2026). Long-term care: up to 80% of after-tax income, minimum $1,507.70 and maximum $4,142.60 a month (2026). Respite/short stay: $49.57 a day (2026).
programs.eligibility_summary: You live in BC with MSP coverage and a health authority assessment shows you need help with daily living because of health or disability. In Victoria, Island Health does the assessment. No doctor referral is needed: you, a family member, or a friend can call the Community Access Line. You must agree to pay the assessed client rate, which can be reduced for hardship.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Island Health Community Access Line (South Island): 1-888-533-2273.
Office of the Seniors Advocate for problems with care or rates: 1-877-952-3181 (see that note).
See 211 (dial 2-1-1) for caregiver support groups.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Call Island Health's Community Access Line for South Island: 1-888-533-2273. Say you (or the person you care for) need help at home.
2. A case manager or intake nurse asks about health and daily needs, then arranges a home assessment.
3. For income-based rates you fill in a financial form (HLTH 1.6) using last year's tax return. If you get GIS or income assistance, say so: home support is free.
4. Services start once the care plan is approved. Ask about respite for caregivers and adult day programs at the same time.
programs.name: Home and Community Care (Island Health): home support, adult day programs, assisted living, long-term care
programs.phone_script: Island Health can send a care aide to help at home, offer adult day programs, and arrange assisted living or a care home. You do not need a doctor's referral; anyone can call the Community Access Line at 1-888-533-2273 to start. If you get the Guaranteed Income Supplement, home support is free; otherwise the cost is based on your income.

programs.amount: Seniors 65 and older get a bigger home owner grant than the basic grant: $845 a year in Victoria. Effective January 1, 2027 the total senior grant is $845 everywhere in BC (the extra $200 for northern and rural homes ends). Homes assessed over $2,075,000 get a reduced grant. Low-income seniors whose home is over the threshold can apply for a supplement, typically $845.
programs.eligibility_summary: You own and live in the home as your principal residence in BC, you are 65 or older in the current year, and the assessed value is at or under the grant threshold ($2,075,000 on the page fetched). You must pay at least $100 in property tax after the grant. The low income grant supplement is for seniors whose home is over the threshold and whose adjusted net income is $32,000 or less (reduced between $30,000 and $32,000).
programs.help_in_victoria:
Home owner grant office: 1-888-355-2700 (toll-free) or 250-387-0555.
Your municipal tax office can read the notice with you; the grant itself is filed with the Province.
See 211 (dial 2-1-1) for in-person help with the online form.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Every year, after your property tax notice arrives, apply for the home owner grant with the Province (not the municipality): online at gov.bc.ca/homeownergrant or by phone at 1-888-355-2700. You need the jurisdiction and roll number from the notice and your Social Insurance Number.
2. Tick the senior (65+) option. You must be 65 or older at some point in the tax year.
3. If your home is over the threshold and your income is $32,000 or less, also file form FIN 65, Home Owner Grant Low Income Supplement Application, by December 31 of the tax year (retroactive for the previous year only).
4. Missed a year? A retroactive grant can be claimed for the previous year.
programs.name: BC Home Owner Grant, additional grant for seniors (and low income supplement)
programs.phone_script: If you're sixty-five or older and own the home you live in, you get a larger home owner grant that takes money off your property tax. You have to apply every year, to the Province, online or by calling 1-888-355-2700. If your home is worth more than about two million dollars and your income is under thirty-two thousand, ask about the low income supplement.

programs.amount: Free flights for the patient and one medically necessary escort, hotel nights (escort shares the room), meal vouchers and Uber rides from the arrival airport. Amounts depend on need; Hope Air reviews each application. Charity, not a government program.
programs.eligibility_summary: You have a confirmed medical appointment far from home that is covered by your provincial health plan (MSP in B.C.), and you are in financial need based on household income, household size and the cost of the trip. Hope Air says income limits vary by province and asks people to apply so their situation can be reviewed.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Hope Air: 1-877-346-4673.
Hospital social workers and specialty clinics can submit the application for you
(hopeair.ca has a referral page for professionals).
Otherwise see 211.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Apply online at https://hopeair.tfaforms.net/wfZeKDW. You can apply yourself, or a family member, friend or your health care team can apply for you.
2. Have your appointment details and household income ready.
3. Questions: call 1-877-346-4673 (Monday to Friday, 6 am to 4:30 pm Pacific) or email info@hopeair.ca.
4. Track an application at https://hopeair.tfaforms.net/5148415.
programs.name: Hope Air (free medical travel)
programs.phone_script: Hope Air is a charity that gives free flights, hotel nights and meals to people who must travel far for a medical appointment and cannot afford it. You need a confirmed appointment covered by MSP. Apply online or call 1-877-346-4673, and apply before you travel.

programs.amount: Free neighbourhood hub in James Bay: services and social programs for seniors 65+, a social prescribing program for 55+, Better at Home (Victoria and Oak Bay), Capital City Volunteers, an income tax clinic, a thrift store, and family and youth programs. Shares its building with the James Bay Urgent and Primary Care Centre.
programs.eligibility_summary: Anyone in the James Bay neighbourhood and nearby, with a focus on seniors, youth, children and families. Seniors outreach is for low-income seniors living on their own without family support. Most services are free.
programs.help_in_victoria:
JBCP: 250-388-7844 ext. 0, 547 Michigan Street.
Better at Home Victoria (run by JBCP): see the Better at Home note.
Or call 211.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Call 250-388-7844, extension 0, or email askus@jbcp.bc.ca.
2. Visit 547 Michigan Street, Victoria (V8V 1S5), Monday to Friday 8 am to 4 pm (closed on statutory holidays).
3. Ask for seniors services, the tax clinic, Better at Home, or a volunteer visit. Staff check what you qualify for and connect you.
programs.name: James Bay Community Project (JBCP)
programs.phone_script: The James Bay Community Project is a neighbourhood centre at 547 Michigan Street that helps seniors, families and youth. For seniors it offers outreach, volunteer help at home, a lunch program and a free tax clinic. Call 250-388-7844, extension 0, Monday to Friday, 8 to 4.

programs.amount: Low-income recreation pass valid for two years. Victoria: unlimited free drop-in at Crystal Pool and public skating at the arena, 52 free drop-ins a year at other regional centres, program credits ($80 per adult, $120 per youth 6-18, $80 per preschooler) and 50% off a regional pass. Saanich: unlimited free drop-in at Saanich centres plus 52 regional visits and $80-$120 credits. Oak Bay: $80 per adult, $120 per child, $80 per preschooler in credit plus 52 free regional drop-ins.
programs.eligibility_summary: You must live in the municipality you apply to (Victoria applicants need a fixed address) and your household's gross income must be at or below the low-income line. For 2025-2026 that is about $29,640 for one person, $38,493 for two, $47,145 for three, $55,076 for four, $62,464 for five, $70,451 for six and $78,436 for seven or more. Applications are confidential.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Crystal Pool and Fitness Centre: 250-361-0732.
Saanich financial assistance: 250-475-5422.
Oak Bay Recreation reception: 250-595-7946.
Victoria Disability Resource Centre, 250-595-0044, can help with the form.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Find your municipality. Victoria: apply at Crystal Pool and Fitness Centre, 250-361-0732, crystalpool@victoria.ca. Saanich: apply online at digital.saanich.ca/life or at any Saanich recreation centre, 250-475-5422, financialassistance@saanich.ca. Oak Bay: bring documents to Oak Bay, Henderson or Monterey Recreation Centre reception, 250-595-7946.
2. Bring photo ID, proof you live there (utility or phone bill or rental agreement from the last three months), and your latest CRA Notice of Assessment or Proof of Income Statement for every adult in the home.
3. Fill in the LIFE application form. Approval is first come, first served and the pass runs two years from the approval date.
4. If you cannot provide the usual documents, ask about an adjudicator form.
programs.name: LIFE program (Leisure Involvement For Everyone) - Victoria, Saanich, Oak Bay
programs.phone_script: The LIFE program gives people on a low income a free two-year recreation pass: free swimming and drop-ins, plus credits for programs. If you live alone and earn under about $29,600 you likely qualify. In Victoria call Crystal Pool at 250-361-0732; in Saanich 250-475-5422; in Oak Bay 250-595-7946.

programs.amount: Non-refundable credit on eligible medical expenses paid in any 12-month period ending in the tax year. For 2025 you claim the part above the lower of 3% of your net income or $2,834. Covers prescriptions, dental, hearing aids, glasses, mobility aids, attendant care, some renovations, travel over 40 km for care, private health plan premiums and much more. Low-income workers may also get the refundable medical expense supplement (line 45200; check current amount).
programs.eligibility_summary: Anyone who paid eligible medical expenses for themselves, their spouse or partner, or their children under 18 (line 33099), or for other dependants such as adult children, parents, grandparents or siblings living in Canada (line 33199). Expenses must not have been reimbursed or claimed in another year. Some items need a prescription, a written certification, or an approved Disability Tax Credit form. It usually pays for the lower-income spouse to make the claim.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Together Against Poverty Society (TAPS), 828 View Street, 250-361-3521 — free year-round tax filing for people with disabilities on low incomes.
CRA individual tax enquiries: 1-800-959-8281.
Or call 211 for free tax clinics.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Collect receipts showing who was paid, plus any prescriptions or certifications.
2. Pick any 12-month period ending in the tax year that gives the biggest total.
3. Enter the total on line 33099 (self, spouse, kids under 18) and the allowable amount for other dependants on line 33199.
4. Subtract the lower of 3% of net income or the yearly cap ($2,834 for 2025).
5. Claim the matching BC credit on line 58689 of Form BC428.
6. Keep receipts; do not send them.
7. If you work and have low income, check line 45200 for the refundable supplement.
programs.name: Medical Expense Tax Credit
programs.phone_script: The medical expense tax credit lowers your income tax for medical costs you paid yourself, like prescriptions, dental work, hearing aids, glasses, mobility aids and attendant care. For 2025 you claim the part above three percent of your income or two thousand eight hundred and thirty-four dollars, whichever is less. Keep your receipts, and a free tax clinic like TAPS at 250-361-3521 can help you claim it.

programs.amount: Refundable credit of 14.5% of up to $50,000 in renovation costs (maximum $7,250) for the 2025 tax year, to build a self-contained suite so a senior aged 65+ or an adult with the Disability Tax Credit can live with family. Paid even if you owe no tax. One claim per qualifying person in their lifetime.
programs.eligibility_summary: You build or convert a self-contained secondary unit (own entrance, kitchen, bathroom, sleeping area) in a home so that a person aged 65 or older, or an adult 18 or older who qualifies for the Disability Tax Credit, can live with a qualifying relative (spouse, parent, grandparent, child, grandchild, sibling, aunt, uncle, niece or nephew, or their spouse). The renovation must be completed in the tax year you claim.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Free tax clinics (CRA Community Volunteer Income Tax Program); see 211. Renovation
claims of this size may need a paid preparer; ask the clinic first.
Seniors Serving Seniors "Seniors Link" line: 250-413-3211, weekdays 9 am to 4 pm
(from sssbc.org).
Canada Revenue Agency: 1-800-959-8281 (TTY 1-800-665-0354).
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Plan the suite to be self-contained and meet local permits and building rules.
2. Keep all receipts and invoices with the contractor's name, address, GST number, dates and description.
3. In the tax year the renovation is finished, complete Schedule 12 (Multigenerational Home Renovation Tax Credit) and enter the credit on line 45355 of your return.
4. The claim can be shared among family members who paid, up to $50,000 in expenses total per renovation.
5. Keep documents in case the CRA asks; do not send them with the return.
programs.name: Multigenerational Home Renovation Tax Credit (MHRTC, line 45355)
programs.phone_script: If you build a self-contained suite in your home so a parent aged 65 or over, or an adult relative with the Disability Tax Credit, can live with you, the Multigenerational Home Renovation Tax Credit gives back 14.5% of up to $50,000 of the cost, up to $7,250, for 2025, even if you owe no tax. You claim it on Schedule 12 of your tax return in the year the suite is finished, and you can only claim it once per person.

programs.amount: Free. MSP pays for doctor visits, hospital care and most medically needed services. Being enrolled is the door to Fair PharmaCare, MSP supplementary benefits, TAP BC, Plan P and the Home Oxygen Program.
programs.eligibility_summary: You must enrol if you live in B.C. and are a Canadian citizen or permanent resident (some work-permit holders also qualify), you make your home in B.C., and you are physically in B.C. at least six months of a calendar year. New arrivals wait the rest of the month they arrived plus two more months before coverage starts.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Health Insurance BC: 1-800-663-7100.
A Service BC office can take the application in person.
For help replacing ID or finding an outreach worker, see 211.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Apply online at gov.bc.ca/AHDC (the BC Application for Health and Drug Coverage), at a Service BC office, or with the paper form.
2. Show primary and secondary identification and have a photo taken at an ICBC driver licensing office for your BC Services Card.
3. Questions or help by phone: Health Insurance BC at 1-800-663-7100 (604-683-7151 in the Lower Mainland).
4. Once enrolled, register for Fair PharmaCare in the same online portal.
programs.name: Medical Services Plan (MSP) enrolment
programs.phone_script: MSP is B.C.'s free public health insurance, and you need it before most other health programs will cover you. If you live in B.C. and are a citizen or permanent resident, apply online at gov.bc.ca slash A-H-D-C, or call Health Insurance BC at 1-800-663-7100. You will need two pieces of ID and a photo taken at an ICBC office.

programs.amount: MSP pays $23 per visit toward a combined 10 visits a year with an approved acupuncturist, chiropractor, massage therapist, naturopath, physical therapist or non-surgical podiatrist (2026). The practitioner may charge more; you pay the difference.
programs.eligibility_summary: You are enrolled in MSP, have lived in Canada for at least 12 months, and your adjusted net family income is under $42,000. Coverage is automatic for people on provincial income or disability assistance, convention refugees, people in long-term care who get the Guaranteed Income Supplement, and inmates. First Nations people with valid BC medical coverage are also covered. Everyone else applies through the Application for Health and Drug Coverage.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Health Insurance BC: 1-800-663-7100.
Help with the AHDC form or tax filing: see 211 (dial 2-1-1).
programs.how_to_apply:
1. File your income tax return; eligibility is checked from your adjusted net income.
2. Apply once with the Application for Health and Drug Coverage at gov.bc.ca/AHDC (online) or by mail to Health Insurance BC, PO Box 9677 Stn Prov Govt, Victoria BC V8W 9P7. The same form also registers you for Fair PharmaCare.
3. If you are on income assistance, PWD, or GIS in long-term care, you do not need to apply.
4. Tell the clinic you have MSP supplementary benefits; they bill MSP for the $23 and charge you the rest. Ask what the visit costs before you book.
programs.name: MSP Supplementary Benefits (physio, chiro, massage, acupuncture, naturopathy, podiatry)
programs.phone_script: If your family income is under forty-two thousand dollars, MSP will pay twenty-three dollars a visit toward up to ten visits a year with a physiotherapist, chiropractor, massage therapist, acupuncturist, naturopath or podiatrist. People on income or disability assistance are covered automatically; everyone else applies once with the Application for Health and Drug Coverage, or call 1-800-663-7100.

programs.amount: Up to $751.97 a month at age 65 to 74 and up to $827.17 a month at 75 and over (July to September 2026 rates). Paid for life. Taxable. Waiting past 65 adds 0.6% a month, up to 36% more at age 70.
programs.eligibility_summary: You are 65 or older, a Canadian citizen or legal resident, and you have lived in Canada for at least 10 years since age 18. You do not need to have worked. You need 40 years in Canada after age 18 for the full amount; fewer years gives a partial pension. If your yearly net income is over $93,454 (2025 income, for July 2026 to June 2027 payments) you pay some back; it stops completely at $152,062 (65 to 74) or $157,923 (75 and over).
programs.help_in_victoria:
Seniors Serving Seniors "Seniors Link" line: 250-413-3211, weekdays 9 am to 4 pm
(volunteer referral agents who know local seniors services; from sssbc.org).
Service Canada: 1-800-277-9914, or visit a Service Canada Centre in person (bring ID).
For other local help with forms, see 211.
Reachable Benefits volunteer navigators can sit with you and fill in the form.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Watch for a letter from Service Canada the month after you turn 64. If it says you are enrolled automatically, you do not need to apply.
2. No letter one month after your 64th birthday? Call Service Canada at 1-800-277-9914 and ask if you need to apply.
3. To apply: sign in to My Service Canada Account and choose "Apply for Old Age Security", or fill in paper form ISP-3550 (Application for the OAS and the GIS) and mail it.
4. Pick a start date. You can start at 65 or delay up to age 70 for a bigger payment. Service Canada says there is no benefit in waiting if you qualify for GIS.
5. File a tax return every year so your pension keeps coming.
programs.name: Old Age Security (OAS) pension
programs.phone_script: Old Age Security is a monthly pension for people 65 and over who have lived in Canada at least 10 years; you do not need to have worked. Right now it pays up to about $752 a month, or $827 once you are 75. Most people are signed up automatically around age 64, but if you never got a letter, call Service Canada at 1-800-277-9914 and ask whether you need to apply.

programs.amount: Free drop-in centre for people who are homeless or living in poverty: three meals a day, showers, free clothing, safe storage for belongings, outreach workers, advocacy, counselling, a free legal clinic, health care, haircuts, and referrals to housing, detox and jobs. Ask the outreach desk about mail, phone and ID help.
programs.eligibility_summary: Anyone who needs it. No ID, income test or referral required. Open seven days a week at 919 Pandora Avenue in downtown Victoria.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Our Place: 919 Pandora Avenue, 250-388-7112.
Cool Aid REES Centre, 465 Swift Street, 250-595-8619, for phones, computers and benefits help.
Or call 211.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Walk in at 919 Pandora Avenue, Victoria (V8V 3P4). The drop-in is open seven days a week (211 lists 6:30 am to 9 pm; the office line is answered 8:30 am to 6:30 pm).
2. Meals: breakfast 7 to 8 am at the nutrition bar, lunch noon to 1 pm, dinner 5 to 6 pm. Showers 8 am to 8:15 pm. Storage 7 to 10:30 am and 5:30 to 8:30 pm.
3. Ask for an outreach worker for help with ID, benefits, housing, mail or a phone.
4. Phone 250-388-7112. Transitional housing intake: men 250-940-5084, women 250-940-5080.
programs.name: Our Place Society
programs.phone_script: Our Place Society is a free drop-in at 919 Pandora Avenue, open every day, with meals, showers, clothing and outreach workers who help with ID, benefits and housing. Breakfast is at 7, lunch at noon, dinner at 5. You can just walk in, or call 250-388-7112.

programs.amount: Lets you move up to 50% of eligible pension income to your spouse on your tax returns to cut the couple's total tax. Each spouse can also claim the $2,000 pension income amount (line 31400) on eligible pension income. Savings depend on the gap between your incomes.
programs.eligibility_summary: You and your spouse or common-law partner both lived in Canada on December 31 and were not separated because of a relationship breakdown for 90 days or more including that date. You received eligible pension income: payments from an employer pension plan at any age, or RRIF, life income fund and RRSP annuity payments if you are 65 or older (or received them because your spouse died). OAS, CPP and GIS cannot be split.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Free tax clinics (CRA Community Volunteer Income Tax Program) for modest incomes; see
211 for locations. Bring both spouses' slips.
Seniors Serving Seniors "Seniors Link" line: 250-413-3211, weekdays 9 am to 4 pm
(from sssbc.org).
Canada Revenue Agency: 1-800-959-8281 (TTY 1-800-665-0354).
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Decide who transfers and who receives. Only one joint election per year.
2. Both of you fill in and sign form T1032, Joint Election to Split Pension Income, with the same numbers.
3. The transferring spouse reports the moved amount as a deduction on line 21000; the receiving spouse reports it as income on line 11600.
4. Split the tax already withheld on that pension in the same proportion (line 43700).
5. File both returns by the due date with T1032 attached (tax software does this). You can change the split each year, and can fix or cancel it within 3 years of the due date.
programs.name: Pension income splitting (form T1032) and the pension income amount
programs.phone_script: If you are a couple and one of you has a bigger pension, you can move up to half of that pension income onto the other person's tax return with form T1032, which can lower the tax you pay together. It works for employer pensions at any age, and for RRIF money once you are 65, but not for CPP or Old Age Security. A free tax clinic can do it when you file.

programs.amount: Single person: $610 support per month instead of $560 (rate table effective August 1, 2023); couple $1,055 instead of $955. Shelter up to $500 single / $695 couple. Monthly earnings exemption $1,080 (2026) instead of $600.
programs.eligibility_summary: You already get income assistance or hardship assistance, you have a health condition that has lasted at least one year (or kept coming back over the past year) and is likely to last at least two more years, and that condition plus other serious barriers make it very hard for you to find or keep work.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Together Against Poverty Society (TAPS), 828 View Street, Victoria. Phone 250-361-3521.
Free advocacy for income assistance and disability benefits.
For other help, call 211.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Be on income assistance or hardship assistance first (apply at My Self Serve or 1-866-866-0800).
2. Ask the ministry for the PPMB application (form HR2892).
3. Fill in your part about your barriers; a doctor or nurse practitioner completes the medical part.
4. Send it back. The ministry will contact you with a decision. If refused, ask for a reconsideration.
programs.name: Persons with Persistent Multiple Barriers (PPMB)
programs.phone_script: PPMB is a step up from regular income assistance for people with a long-term health problem and other big barriers to work. It pays a little more, lets you keep more from a job, and adds dental and health coverage. Ask the ministry for form HR2892 at 1-866-866-0800, or call TAPS in Victoria at 250-361-3521 for free help with it.

programs.amount: A low-interest loan from the Province that pays your property taxes for you. Regular Program interest is 6.45% a year for 2026 (the government's prime rate of 4.45% plus 2%, per the rate table row for July 1 to September 30, 2026). Before 2026 the rate was prime minus 2%. The loan is repaid when the home is sold or transferred. Not a grant: the taxes are still owed.
programs.eligibility_summary: You are 55 or older this year, or a surviving spouse of any age, or a person with disabilities; you are a Canadian citizen or permanent resident who has lived in BC for at least one year; the home is your principal residence; you have at least 25% equity in it (all mortgages and charges plus the deferred taxes cannot be more than 75% of the BC Assessment value); and all earlier years' property taxes, utility fees, penalties and interest are paid.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Property tax deferment office: 1-888-355-2700 (toll-free) or 250-387-0555 (Victoria).
Your municipality's property tax counter (City of Victoria, Saanich, etc.) can explain the tax notice but the deferment application goes to the Province.
See 211 (dial 2-1-1) for a seniors' organisation that can help with the online form.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Wait for your property tax notice (in Victoria it usually arrives in late May).
2. Claim your home owner grant first (see the home owner grant note).
3. Apply online through eTaxBC at gov.bc.ca (search "defer property taxes"). You will need your folio/roll number from the tax notice and your Social Insurance Number. If you cannot use a computer, call 1-888-355-2700 for help.
4. Apply before the tax due date shown on your notice to avoid late penalties.
5. Each year you must renew; the Province sends a Statement of Account. Check the renewal page or call to confirm the current renewal steps.
programs.name: BC Property Tax Deferment (55+, surviving spouse, persons with disabilities)
programs.phone_script: If you're fifty-five or older and own your home, BC can pay your property taxes for you as a low-interest loan, and you pay it back only when the house is sold. The interest rate for 2026 is six point four five percent, and it can change each period. You need at least twenty-five percent equity and you apply online after the tax notice arrives; the deferment office is at 1-888-355-2700.

programs.amount: Single person: $983.50 support + shelter up to $500 + $52 transportation supplement per month (rates effective December 1, 2025). You can earn up to $16,200 a year (2026) before it lowers your cheque.
programs.eligibility_summary: You are 18 or older (you can start at 17 and a half), live in B.C., have little income and assets (under $100,000 for a single person), and have a severe physical or mental impairment that is expected to last more than two years. It must greatly limit your daily living activities so that you need help from a person, a device or an assistance animal.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Together Against Poverty Society (TAPS), 828 View Street, Victoria. Phone 250-361-3521.
Free legal advocacy for provincial disability benefits and income assistance. Open Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday 9 am to noon and 1 pm to 4 pm; Wednesday phone only.
Disability Alliance BC, Advocacy Access Program, toll-free 1-800-663-1278,
advocacy@dabc.ca. Helps with PWD applications and appeals across B.C.
For other help, call 211.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Apply for assistance online at My Self Serve or call 1-866-866-0800 to show you qualify financially.
2. Ask the ministry for the PWD Designation Application.
3. Fill in your own section (Section 1).
4. Your doctor or nurse practitioner fills in the medical report (Section 2).
5. A prescribed professional (doctor, nurse, social worker, occupational therapist and others) fills in the assessor report (Section 3).
6. Send the whole form back. If refused, you can ask for a reconsideration and then appeal.
programs.name: Persons with Disabilities (PWD) designation and Disability Assistance
programs.phone_script: PWD is B.C.'s disability status: if you get it, you get a monthly disability assistance payment and a free bus pass, and you can earn some money from work without losing it. To apply, you fill in one section, your doctor fills in one, and another professional fills in the third. Call 1-866-866-0800 to start, or TAPS in Victoria at 250-361-3521 for free help.

programs.amount: Dental up to $1,000 every two calendar years; eye exam up to $48.90 every two years plus glasses at the ministry rate; diet supplements $15 to $80 a month by diet type (rate table effective August 1, 2023); Monthly Nutritional Supplement up to $180 plus $45 a month; medical equipment and medical travel paid with pre-approval.
programs.eligibility_summary: You receive disability assistance (PWD), or in most cases income assistance, hardship assistance or Medical Services Only, and the item is medically needed, you have no other way to pay for it, and the ministry approves it before you buy it.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Together Against Poverty Society (TAPS), 828 View Street, Victoria. Phone 250-361-3521.
Free advocacy for provincial disability benefits, including refused supplements.
Disability Alliance BC, Advocacy Access, toll-free 1-800-663-1278.
For other help, call 211.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Always get pre-approval first. Call 1-866-866-0800 or visit a ministry office before buying anything.
2. Dental and optical: tell the dentist or eye clinic you are on assistance and show your BC Services Card; they bill the ministry through Pacific Blue Cross.
3. Diet supplement: form HR3635, confirmed by a doctor, nurse practitioner or registered dietitian.
4. Monthly Nutritional Supplement: form HR2847, medical part signed by a doctor, nurse practitioner or dietitian.
5. Medical equipment: bring a prescription or an occupational or physical therapist's assessment; the ministry pays for the least expensive item that meets the need.
6. Medical transportation: ask before travelling and keep receipts.
programs.name: PWD health supplements (dental, optical, medical equipment, diet, transportation)
programs.phone_script: If you are on B.C. disability assistance, you can get extra help for dental work, glasses, special diets, medical equipment and travel to medical appointments. The key rule is to call the ministry at 1-866-866-0800 and get approval before you spend anything. If you are turned down, TAPS in Victoria at 250-361-3521 can help you appeal.

programs.amount: Monthly cash help with rent for working families with children. It pays back part of the rent above 30% of your income. Rent counted up to $1,950 a month (family of 3 or less) or $2,200 (family of 4 or more) - rent ceilings effective April 2025.
programs.eligibility_summary: Families in BC with at least one dependent child, a household income of $60,000 a year or less before tax, less than $100,000 in assets, who pay more than 30% of their income on rent, have lived in BC for 12 months, and are not on income or disability assistance.
programs.help_in_victoria: Together Against Poverty Society (TAPS), 828 View Street, Victoria. Phone 250-361-3521. TAPS gives free help with tenancy problems and income assistance. For other local help, dial 2-1-1.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Get the RAP application form from bchousing.org, by mail, or in person at a BC Housing office.
2. Attach proof of income (tax return), proof you live in BC, proof of rent, bank details for direct deposit, and proof of assets. Add proof of full-time studies for a child 19 to 24.
3. Send it in: upload online, drop it off, fax 604-439-4729, or mail it.
4. If approved, money goes to your bank account on the last working day of each month.
programs.name: BC Rental Assistance Program (RAP)
programs.phone_script: The BC Rental Assistance Program gives working families with children money each month to help pay rent. You may qualify if your household earned $60,000 or less last year and more than 30% of your income goes to rent. You can apply through BC Housing at 1-800-257-7756, and I can note a callback if you'd like help with the form.

programs.amount: Savings plan with free government money. Bond: up to $1,000 a year (lifetime $20,000) with no deposit needed if 2026 family income is $38,237 or less; partial bond up to $58,523. Grant: government matches deposits at $3 per $1 on the first $500 and $2 per $1 on the next $1,000 when family income is $117,045 or less (2026), up to $3,500 a year and $70,000 lifetime; $1 per $1 on the first $1,000 above that income. Unclaimed grant and bond can be caught up for the past 10 years.
programs.eligibility_summary: The person the plan is for (the beneficiary) must be approved for the Disability Tax Credit, live in Canada, have a Social Insurance Number, and open the plan before December 31 of the year they turn 59. Grants and bonds are paid until the end of the year they turn 49. The amount of grant and bond depends on family income from two years earlier: the beneficiary's own income (plus spouse) from age 19, or the parents' income before that.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Victoria Disability Resource Centre, 817A Fort Street, 250-595-0044 — information and referral for disability benefits.
Canada Disability Savings Program (Service Canada): 1-866-204-0357.
Or call 211 for other options.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Get approved for the Disability Tax Credit.
2. Make sure you have a SIN and have filed tax returns for the last two years.
3. Pick a bank or credit union that offers RDSPs (the government publishes a list; you do not need an existing account there).
4. Open the plan and, at the same time, sign the application for the Canada Disability Savings Grant and Bond.
5. The bond arrives every year on its own. To get the grant, deposit money; $1,500 a year gets the full grant at lower incomes.
6. Ask about catching up on past years if you were DTC-eligible before.
programs.name: Registered Disability Savings Plan (RDSP) with the Canada Disability Savings Grant and Bond
programs.phone_script: An RDSP is a savings plan for people who have the Disability Tax Credit. If your income is low, the government puts up to a thousand dollars a year into it even if you deposit nothing, and it matches any money you do put in. You open one at a bank or credit union, and you can call 1-866-204-0357 to ask questions.

programs.amount: Short-term loans of walkers, wheelchairs, bath seats, commodes and similar equipment on a donation basis. HELP Plus (with the health authority) lends hospital beds and patient lifts. The Red Cross pages fetched do not state a fixed loan length; check current terms when you call.
programs.eligibility_summary: Anyone recovering from illness or injury, with a mobility problem, going home from hospital, or in palliative care. You need a referral form from a health professional such as a doctor, physiotherapist, occupational therapist, nurse or chiropractor (the Red Cross Referral Form on the Victoria office page).
programs.help_in_victoria:
Red Cross Victoria office, 909 Fairfield Road: 250-382-2043 (fax 250-382-3449),
Monday to Friday 9:30 am to 4:30 pm.
Island Health Community Access line (South Island): 250-388-2273 or 1-888-533-2273,
8:30 am to 10:30 pm, seven days a week (islandhealth.ca), for HELP Plus referrals and home care assessment.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Ask a health professional to complete the Red Cross Referral Form (link on the Victoria office page).
2. Call the Victoria depot at 250-382-2043 before you go, to confirm it is open and the item is in stock.
3. Pick up at 909 Fairfield Road, Victoria, Monday to Friday 9:30 am to 4:30 pm. Staff bring equipment to the door.
4. For hospital beds or lifts (HELP Plus), the hospital or Island Health home care team makes the referral.
5. Return the equipment when you no longer need it; ask for an extension form if you need longer.
programs.name: Red Cross Health Equipment Loan Program (HELP), Victoria
programs.phone_script: The Red Cross lends walkers, wheelchairs and bathroom aids for free, by donation. You need a referral form signed by a doctor, nurse, physio or occupational therapist. Then call the Victoria office at 250-382-2043 and pick up at 909 Fairfield Road, weekdays 9:30 to 4:30.

programs.amount: A monthly cash payment toward rent for renters aged 60 and over. It pays part of the gap between 30% of your gross income and your rent, up to a rent ceiling of $1,150 a month (as of April 2025). The exact amount depends on your income and rent.
programs.eligibility_summary: You are 60 or older, you rent your home in BC, you have lived in BC for the last 12 months, and your gross household income is under $40,000 a year ($3,333.34 a month). You pay more than 30% of your gross monthly household income on rent. You must be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident, or in one of a few refugee or CUAET categories, and not under sponsorship.
programs.help_in_victoria:
BC Housing SAFER line: 1-800-257-7756.
For help filling out the form in person, see 211 (dial 2-1-1) for a seniors' centre or community agency near you.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Gather: your rent amount (lease or rent receipt), proof of age, and last year's income (Notice of Assessment or CRA proof of income for everyone in the household).
2. Apply to BC Housing online or with the paper SAFER form. Call 1-800-257-7756 (or 604-433-2218) to have a form mailed or to ask questions.
3. Everyone in the household who is 19 or older signs.
4. BC Housing calculates the payment and pays it monthly, usually by direct deposit. Report changes in rent or income.
programs.name: Shelter Aid for Elderly Renters (SAFER)
programs.phone_script: If you're sixty or older, rent your home, and spend more than thirty percent of your income on rent, BC Housing's SAFER program can send you money every month toward the rent. Your household income has to be under forty thousand dollars a year. You can apply by calling BC Housing at 1-800-257-7756.

programs.amount: Free information and referral line for seniors and caregivers. The office is independent of government departments, monitors seniors' services (health care, housing, income support, community support, transportation) and reports on systemic problems. It is not a court or complaints tribunal, but its specialists help you find the right door and track concerns.
programs.eligibility_summary: Any senior, family member, caregiver, or service provider in BC can call. There is no eligibility test. The office helps with questions about long-term care, home support, assisted living, housing, income programs, transportation, and where to complain when something goes wrong.
programs.help_in_victoria:
The office is in Victoria: 250-952-3181 or 1-877-952-3181.
For local seniors' services, Seniors Serving Seniors (see that note) and 211.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Call the information and referral line: 1-877-952-3181 (toll-free) or 250-952-3181 in Victoria, Monday to Friday 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.
2. Or email info@seniorsadvocatebc.ca, or write to PO Box 9651, STN PROV GOV, Victoria BC V8W 9P4.
3. A senior service specialist listens, explains options, and refers you to the agency that can act (health authority patient care quality office, Residential Tenancy Branch, BC Housing, and so on).
4. Your concern is logged; patterns feed the Advocate's public reports and recommendations.
programs.name: Office of the Seniors Advocate of BC
programs.phone_script: The Office of the Seniors Advocate has a free information line for seniors and caregivers in BC. They can explain care home fees, home support, housing and income programs, and tell you exactly where to complain if something has gone wrong. Call 1-877-952-3181 weekdays between eight-thirty and four-thirty.

programs.amount: Refundable credit of 10% of eligible home renovation costs, up to $10,000 of costs a year, so a maximum of $1,000 back per tax year.
programs.eligibility_summary: You lived in BC on December 31 of the tax year and you are 65 or older, or you live with a family member who is 65 or older, or you (or a family member who lives with you) qualify for the federal Disability Tax Credit. The renovation must make the home safer or easier to get around in, for example grab bars, a walk-in tub, a ramp, or wider doorways.
programs.help_in_victoria:
CRA individual tax enquiries: 1-800-959-8281.
BC tax questions: 1-877-387-3332.
Free tax clinics for people with modest income: see 211 (dial 2-1-1).
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Keep every receipt from contractors and suppliers. Receipts must show what was done and where.
2. When you file your tax return, fill in Schedule BC(S12), the BC Home Renovation Tax Credit for Seniors and Persons with Disabilities form.
3. Carry the amount to box 60480 on form BC479 in your return. A free tax clinic can do this for you.
4. You can still claim it if you have no tax to pay: it is refundable, so the money is paid to you.
programs.name: BC Home Renovation Tax Credit for Seniors and Persons with Disabilities
programs.phone_script: If you or someone you live with is sixty-five or older, or has the Disability Tax Credit, BC gives back ten percent of what you spend on safety renovations like grab bars, ramps, or a walk-in tub, up to a thousand dollars a year. You claim it on your tax return with form BC(S12). Keep your receipts.

programs.amount: Free information and referral for seniors in Greater Victoria. Runs the Seniors Link phone line, a directory of local seniors' services, and a Return to Health program. A registered charity run largely by senior volunteers.
programs.eligibility_summary: Any senior, family member or caregiver in Greater Victoria can call. There is no age or income test. It is the local place to ask "who does what for seniors in Victoria" and to be pointed to housing, care, benefits, transportation and social programs.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Seniors Serving Seniors, Seniors Link: 250-413-3211, 602-620 View Street.
Backup: 211 (dial 2-1-1) and the Office of the Seniors Advocate 1-877-952-3181.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Call the Seniors Link line at 250-413-3211. (The Return to Health program has its own line: 236-464-7172.)
2. Or email ed@sssbc.org, or visit the office at 602-620 View Street, Victoria BC V8W 1J6.
3. Explain what you need; a volunteer or staff member gives information and referrals to local services.
4. Ask for the printed seniors' service directory if you prefer paper.
programs.name: Seniors Serving Seniors (Victoria)
programs.phone_script: Seniors Serving Seniors is a Victoria charity run by seniors that helps other seniors find local services. Their Seniors Link phone line is 250-413-3211, and their office is at 620 View Street downtown. Call them when you're not sure who to ask.

programs.amount: Up to $99.30 a month for a single senior, up to $110.25 each for a couple who both get GIS, up to $99.83 for a spouse on the federal Allowance (rate table effective July 1, 2026). Most people get less than the maximum; the amount shrinks as other income rises.
programs.eligibility_summary: You live in BC and you get Old Age Security (OAS) plus the Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS), or you are 60 to 64 and get the federal Allowance. You have little or no other taxable income. Nobody applies: the Province pays it automatically to people whose federal GIS or Allowance amount shows they qualify.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Ministry of Social Development and Poverty Reduction: 1-866-866-0800.
For the GIS side (Service Canada), see the GIS note in this knowledge base.
Local help with tax filing so GIS keeps flowing: see 211 (dial 2-1-1) for free tax clinics.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Make sure you are getting OAS and GIS (or the Allowance) from Service Canada. That is the only door in.
2. File your income tax return every year, even with no income. GIS is renewed from your tax return, and the Supplement follows GIS.
3. Nothing else to do. The money arrives with your OAS/GIS payment, the same way (direct deposit or cheque), on the federal payment dates.
4. If you get GIS but no Supplement, call the Ministry of Social Development and Poverty Reduction at 1-866-866-0800 (Monday to Friday, 9 am to 4 pm).
programs.name: BC Senior's Supplement
programs.phone_script: If you get the Guaranteed Income Supplement and live in BC, the Province adds a small monthly top-up called the Senior's Supplement, up to about ninety-nine dollars a month for a single person. You don't apply for it; it comes automatically with your OAS payment. The key is to get GIS and file your taxes every year.

programs.amount: In-person BC government office for the Medical Services Plan (MSP), BC Services Card setup and identity checks, income assistance applications, birth and marriage certificates, driver's licences and BC ID (through ICBC), residential tenancy forms and government payments. Free. Help by phone through the provincial line 1-800-663-7867.
programs.eligibility_summary: Anyone who needs to deal with a BC government program in person. No appointment needed for most services. Bring ID. The provincial phone line can do much of the same work if you cannot travel.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Service BC Victoria: 403-771 Vernon Avenue, 250-387-6121.
Province-wide line: 1-800-663-7867.
TAPS, 250-361-3521, for advocacy on income assistance and PWD.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Visit 403-771 Vernon Avenue, Victoria (near Uptown), Monday to Friday 9 am to 4:30 pm. Phone 250-387-6121 or email ServiceBC.Victoria@gov.bc.ca.
2. Or call the province-wide Service BC line at 1-800-663-7867 (Victoria 250-387-6121) and ask to be connected to the program you need.
3. Bring your BC Services Card or other ID and any letters or forms.
programs.name: Service BC Centre - Victoria
programs.phone_script: Service BC is the provincial government counter. In Victoria it's at 771 Vernon Avenue, Suite 403, near Uptown, open Monday to Friday, 9 to 4:30. They help with MSP, the BC Services Card, income assistance forms and birth certificates. Or call 1-800-663-7867.

programs.amount: In-person federal government office for CPP, Old Age Security, GIS, CPP Disability, Employment Insurance, Social Insurance Numbers, passports, the Canadian Dental Care Plan and other federal programs. Free. Staff help you apply, check on an application, or fix a problem with a payment.
programs.eligibility_summary: Anyone. No appointment is needed for most services. Bring government ID (and your SIN if you have one). If you cannot get downtown, most of the same help is available by phone on the toll-free lines below.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Service Canada Victoria: 1150 Douglas Street, 4th floor, Suite 450.
By phone: 1-800-277-9914 (pensions), 1-800-622-6232 (general).
Victoria Disability Resource Centre, 250-595-0044, helps fill in CPP-D and OAS/GIS forms.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Visit 1150 Douglas Street, 4th Floor, Suite 450, Victoria (V8W 3M9), Monday to Friday 8:30 am to 4 pm.
2. Or call: CPP, OAS and GIS 1-800-277-9914; Employment Insurance 1-800-206-7218; Social Insurance Number 1-866-274-6627; passports 1-800-567-6868; general questions 1 800 O-Canada (1-800-622-6232); TTY 1-800-926-9105.
3. Bring ID, your SIN, banking details for direct deposit, and any letters you received.
4. There is also a Victoria West Shore Service Canada Centre for people on the West Shore.
programs.name: Service Canada Centre - Victoria
programs.phone_script: Service Canada's Victoria office is downtown at 1150 Douglas Street, on the 4th floor, open Monday to Friday, 8:30 to 4. They handle Canada Pension Plan, Old Age Security, GIS, disability pensions and EI. If you can't go in, call 1-800-277-9914 for pensions or 1-800-622-6232 for anything else.

programs.amount: Two seniors' activity centres (Victoria and Saanich) with low-cost programs, meals and social events, plus an Outreach program that visits seniors where they live to connect them with services. Membership fee: check current amount.
programs.eligibility_summary: Older adults in Greater Victoria. Programs and meals may have small fees; the Outreach program that brings information to seniors' buildings is free. No income test.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Silver Threads Victoria: 250-388-4268. Saanich: 250-382-3151.
Seniors Serving Seniors line: 250-413-3211.
Or call 211.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Call the centre nearest you: Victoria Centre, 1911 Quadra Street (V8T 4C1), 250-388-4268; or Saanich Centre, 286 Hampton Road (V8Z 1H1), 250-382-3151.
2. Both are open Monday to Friday, 9 am to 3:30 pm.
3. Ask for the program guide, food services, or the Outreach worker.
4. Building managers can also ask Outreach to hold an information session in their building.
programs.name: Silver Threads Service (seniors' centres)
programs.phone_script: Silver Threads runs two seniors' centres, one at 1911 Quadra Street in Victoria and one at 286 Hampton Road in Saanich, with activities, meals and an outreach worker who can visit your building. Call 250-388-4268 for the Victoria centre or 250-382-3151 for Saanich, Monday to Friday, 9 to 3:30.

programs.amount: $31 processing fee per permit (waived on request if you cannot afford it). A permanent permit lasts three years and is renewable.
programs.eligibility_summary: You cannot walk any distance without another person or a mobility aid, cannot walk 100 metres without risk to your health, or have a disability that affects your ability to walk. Some permits are also issued for people who are blind or Deaf, or where safety is a concern. A medical professional with an MSP number must confirm this.
programs.help_in_victoria: Call 211 for a local agency that can help with the form. SPARC BC itself is in Burnaby: 1-888-718-7794.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Get the SPARC BC Parking Permit Application from sparc.bc.ca (or apply online at online.sparc.bc.ca).
2. Fill in your part and have a medical professional with a valid MSP number complete the medical section.
3. Send it with the $31 fee (ask for the hardship waiver if you cannot pay) to SPARC BC, 4445 Norfolk Street, Burnaby BC V5G 0A7.
4. Allow 2 to 3 weeks for processing.
programs.name: SPARC BC accessible parking permit
programs.phone_script: The accessible parking permit comes from SPARC BC. If walking short distances is hard or risky for you, a doctor or other medical professional signs the form, you send it with a thirty-one dollar fee, and the permit arrives in two to three weeks. If you cannot afford the fee, ask SPARC for hardship help at 1-888-718-7794.

programs.amount: Discounts from partner carriers when you must travel out of town for medical care: BC Ferries waives the fare for the patient, escort and a regular passenger car; Harbour Air, Helijet, Seair and Pacific Coastal about 30% off economy fares; VIA Rail 30%; VI Connector 25%; BC Ferries Connector bus 15 to 20%; NOW Shuttle 33% (companion free). No cash, and no refund for travel already taken. Figures from the gov.bc.ca partner list read 2026-09-01.
programs.eligibility_summary: You are a B.C. resident enrolled in MSP, a doctor or nurse practitioner has referred you to a non-emergency specialist service that is not available in your community, and you are not covered by third-party insurance for the trip. An escort is covered only if the patient is 18 or under or cannot travel alone for medical reasons.
programs.help_in_victoria:
TAP line: 1-800-661-2668, 24 hours.
Your referring clinic or hospital social worker can complete the form.
For other travel help, see 211.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Ask your doctor, nurse practitioner or the specialty clinic for the TAP form. They fill in most of it.
2. Call 1-800-661-2668 (24 hours a day, 7 days a week) with your Personal Health Number to get a confirmation number.
3. Show the completed form with the confirmation number to the ferry, airline or bus when you book or board.
4. Use the form within 90 days of the appointment date. Each form is for one trip.
programs.name: Travel Assistance Program (TAP BC)
programs.phone_script: If you have to leave town for a specialist, TAP BC gives you discounts on BC Ferries, some airlines and buses. Ask the clinic that referred you for the TAP form, then call 1-800-661-2668 for a confirmation number before you travel. It does not pay for hotels or meals, and it cannot refund a trip you already took.

programs.amount: Free legal advocacy for income assistance, BC disability benefits (PWD) and residential tenancy problems, plus free year-round income tax filing. Drop-in, no appointment needed.
programs.eligibility_summary: Anyone in Greater Victoria who needs help with income assistance, the PWD designation, a ministry denial or reconsideration, or a problem with their landlord. The tax service is for people with a modest income and a simple tax situation. No cost.
programs.help_in_victoria:
TAPS, 828 View Street, 250-361-3521.
Burnside Gorge Community Centre (471 Cecelia Road, 250-388-5251) is a drop-off point for TAPS tax filing.
Or call 211.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Drop in at 828 View Street, Victoria (V8W 1K2), Monday, Tuesday, Thursday or Friday, 9 am to noon and 1 pm to 4 pm. No appointment needed.
2. Or call 250-361-3521. On Wednesdays the office is phone-only (closed to walk-ins) but phones are answered 9 to noon and 1 to 4.
3. Bring your ID, any letters from the ministry or your landlord, and for taxes your tax slips and last year's Notice of Assessment.
programs.name: Together Against Poverty Society (TAPS)
programs.phone_script: TAPS, the Together Against Poverty Society, gives free help in Victoria with income assistance, disability benefits and landlord problems, and they file taxes for free all year. You can just walk in at 828 View Street, Monday, Tuesday, Thursday or Friday, 9 to noon or 1 to 4. Their phone number is 250-361-3521.

programs.amount: Tax-free. Either Pain and Suffering Compensation (a lifetime monthly payment or a lump sum, your choice) or, for Second World War and Korean War service or claims made before April 2006, a Disability Pension (lifetime monthly, more if you have a spouse or children). The amount depends on how much the condition is linked to service and how severe it is. Rates are published on veterans.gc.ca; check current amount.
programs.eligibility_summary: You are a current or former member of the Canadian Armed Forces or the RCMP, a Second World War or Korean War veteran (including Merchant Navy), or one of certain Second World War civilians, and you have a diagnosed medical condition or disability that you can show is related to your service. Hearing loss, tinnitus, PTSD, joint injuries and Gulf War Illness are common examples.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Veterans Affairs Canada: 1-866-522-2122, or any VAC office or Service Canada office.
Royal Canadian Legion and War Amps service officers help with claims for free; see 211 for the nearest branch.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Sign in or register for My VAC Account and use the guided online form, or download the paper form and drop it at a VAC office, CAF Transition Centre or Service Canada office, or mail it.
2. Gather your diagnosis and evidence linking it to service; VAC uses medical questionnaires and its Table of Disabilities.
3. Free help is available from VAC staff at 1-866-522-2122, and from Service Officers at the Royal Canadian Legion or The War Amps.
4. If refused, ask for a departmental review or appeal.
5. If your condition gets worse, ask for a reassessment.
programs.name: Veterans Affairs Canada disability benefits (pointer)
programs.phone_script: If you served in the Canadian Forces or the RCMP and have a health condition related to your service, Veterans Affairs Canada pays a tax-free disability benefit. You can apply online through My VAC Account or with free help from the Legion or by calling 1-866-522-2122. The amount depends on how the condition is linked to your service and how serious it is.

programs.amount: Free services for people who are homeless or at risk: the REES Centre downtown with drop-in phones and computers, peer support, help applying for income and disability benefits, referrals and housing-retention support; plus emergency shelters, a community health centre, dental clinic, meals and affordable housing.
programs.eligibility_summary: Anyone in Greater Victoria who is homeless, at risk of homelessness, or living on a very low income. Drop-in; no referral needed for the REES Centre. Shelter and housing have their own intake.
programs.help_in_victoria:
Cool Aid REES Centre: 465 Swift Street, 250-595-8619.
Our Place Society: 919 Pandora Avenue, 250-388-7112.
Or call 211.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. REES Centre: drop in at 465 Swift Street, Victoria, Monday to Friday 9 am to 3:30 pm (closed weekends and holidays), or call 250-595-8619. Use the phones and computers, ask an outreach worker for help with benefits, ID or housing.
2. Free clothing room at REES: Tuesdays 9:30 to 11:30 am.
3. For shelter, health or housing, call the main office at 250-383-1977 (101-749 Pandora Avenue, V8W 1N9).
programs.name: Victoria Cool Aid Society (REES Centre and services)
programs.phone_script: Cool Aid's REES Centre at 465 Swift Street is a free drop-in with phones, computers and outreach workers who help you apply for income and disability benefits and find housing. It's open Monday to Friday, 9 to 3:30; call 250-595-8619. Cool Aid's main office is 250-383-1977.

programs.amount: Free information, referral and one-on-one help applying for disability benefits (PWD, DTC, CPP-D and others), peer support groups, accessible parking permits (SPARC), and disability awareness training.
programs.eligibility_summary: Anyone in Greater Victoria who has a disability, or who supports someone who does. No cost, no income test. Many staff and volunteers have disabilities themselves.
programs.help_in_victoria:
VDRC, 817A Fort Street, 250-595-0044.
TAPS, 828 View Street, 250-361-3521 (income assistance and PWD appeals).
Or call 211.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Call 250-595-0044 or drop in at 817A Fort Street, Victoria (V8W 1H6).
2. Hours: Monday to Thursday 9 am to 4 pm, Friday 9 am to 2 pm.
3. Say what you need: help with a benefit form, a parking permit, peer support, or just finding the right service.
4. Bring ID and any forms or letters you already have.
programs.name: Victoria Disability Resource Centre (VDRC)
programs.phone_script: The Victoria Disability Resource Centre is a free drop-in centre downtown at 817A Fort Street. They help people with disabilities apply for benefits, get a parking permit, and find peer support. Call them at 250-595-0044, Monday to Thursday 9 to 4, or Friday 9 to 2.

programs.amount: Free, culturally safe services for Indigenous people in Greater Victoria: a primary care clinic, housing and homelessness help, food security, family and children's services, employment and education support, and cultural programs.
programs.eligibility_summary: Indigenous people (First Nations, Metis and Inuit) living in or visiting Greater Victoria, whether or not they have status. Many programs are open to all. No cost.
programs.help_in_victoria:
VNFC reception: 250-384-3211.
BCANDS (Indigenous Disability Canada), Victoria, for DTC and RDSP help: 250-381-7303 or 1-888-815-5511.
Or call 211.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Call reception at 250-384-3211 or visit 231 Regina Avenue, Victoria (V8Z 1J6), Monday to Friday 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.
2. For the Primary Care Clinic call 250-940-2669 (Unit 209, 2951 Tillicum Road; Monday to Friday 9:30 am to 3 pm).
3. For the shelter call 250-886-1360 between 2 pm and 7 pm for an assessment.
4. Tell reception what you need and they will connect you with the right program or worker.
programs.name: Victoria Native Friendship Centre (VNFC)
programs.phone_script: The Victoria Native Friendship Centre offers free, culturally safe services for Indigenous people: a health clinic, housing help, food, family programs and more. It's at 231 Regina Avenue, near Tillicum. Call reception at 250-384-3211, Monday to Friday, 8:30 to 4:30.

programs.amount: Free settlement help for immigrants and refugees in Greater Victoria: the BC Newcomer Services Program, English classes, help understanding government benefits and finances (Financial Well-Being), employment programs, and digital literacy classes for BIPOC seniors.
programs.eligibility_summary: Immigrants, refugees and other newcomers living in Greater Victoria and Vancouver Island, including permanent residents, refugee claimants and, for some programs, naturalized citizens and temporary residents. Seniors who came to Canada years ago are welcome. Free.
programs.help_in_victoria:
VIRCS: 1004 North Park Street, 250-361-9433.
Inter-Cultural Association of Greater Victoria is the other main settlement agency (call 211 for the number).
Or call 211.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Call 250-361-9433 or visit 1004 North Park Street, Victoria (V8T 1C6).
2. Ask for a settlement worker. They help with benefit applications (OAS, GIS, MSP, income assistance), forms, translation and referrals.
3. Bring your immigration documents and ID.
4. Hours were not listed on the page fetched: check when you call.
programs.name: Victoria Immigrant and Refugee Centre Society (VIRCS)
programs.phone_script: The Victoria Immigrant and Refugee Centre helps newcomers with settlement, English classes, jobs and understanding government benefits, all for free. It's at 1004 North Park Street. Call 250-361-9433 and ask for a settlement worker.

programs.amount: Pays all or part of the cost of assistive devices, ergonomic equipment, hearing and communication devices, workplace changes, vehicle modifications for work, and ASL interpreting, depending on your financial situation. No published dollar cap.
programs.eligibility_summary: You live in B.C., are legally allowed to work here, are 16 or older, are not a full-time student (unless in your last year), and you have a work-related barrier from a disability or functional limitation that assistive equipment or disability supports would remove so you can start work, keep your job, or take part in training or volunteering.
programs.help_in_victoria:
WorkBC Assistive Technology Services, Victoria: 817A Fort Street, Victoria BC V8W 1H6.
Phone 1-844-453-5506, assistivetechnologyservices@workbc.ca.
For other help, call 211.
programs.how_to_apply:
1. Apply through WorkBC Online Employment Services (apply.workbc.ca) and ask for Assistive Technology Services, or call 1-844-453-5506.
2. WorkBC reviews your application and tells you if you are eligible.
3. An assessment identifies the equipment or supports you need; WorkBC arranges purchase and setup.
programs.name: WorkBC Assistive Technology Services
programs.phone_script: WorkBC Assistive Technology Services pays for the equipment you need to work with a disability, like a special keyboard, a hearing device, an ergonomic chair, or changes to your workplace or vehicle. It is for people working, looking for work, or volunteering. The Victoria office is on Fort Street; call 1-844-453-5506 to apply.
